(Sironcha) kuțța pillar, post. Pkt. khunța- peg. H. khūtā stump, stake, post, peg; . Mar. khūță, khūți stake, peg. Turner, s.v. khuţțo, khuțți.

Ta. kuttakai contract of lease. Ma. kuttaka farm, contract (as for liquor, honey, wax), monopoly. Ko. guti'g government contract. Ka. guttă, gutte exclusive right of sale, farm, monopoly; guttige id., rental on land. Tu. guttige liquor-shop; guttedāre holder of a monopoly, a liquor contractor, Te. gutta lease. [Skt. kuttā a type of 'farminglease' in South India (J. Duncan M. Derrett, BSOAS 21.61-81). H. guttā exclusive right of sale, monopoly, contract, lease. Or. kuta appraisement of the produce of a field, tree, or tank (ib. 62, n. 2). Derrett takes = khũți peg. DICTIONARY 25 manure. the words to be Dravidian in origin, since the legal institution is South Indian.

Ta. kuppācam coat, bodice, jacket. Ma. kuppayam jacket, gown, robe. Ko. kupa'cm (kupa ct) coat, men's special dancing dress with full skirt. To. kuposm (kupost-) coat. Ka. kuppasa, kub(b)asa, kubusa jacket. Kod. kuppia Coorg man's coat. Tu. kuppasa petticoat, bodice. Te. kup(p)asamu, kubusamu, (K also) kūsamu half-jacket, woman's bodice. Kol. kubasam bodice. Nk. kubaśam id. /Skt. kůrpása- cuirass, quilted jacket worn as armor; kūrpāsaka- bodice, jacket (worn esp. by women), cuirass, corselet. Pkt. kuppāsa-, kuppisa- id. (P. Thieme, ZDMG 91.90f., 92.52; H. W Bailey, Donum natalicum H. S. Nyberg oblatum 10f.).

Ta. kuppi cowdung. Ko. ko.ba:rm (obl. ko ba.rt-) To. kuborm (obl. kubort-) id. Ka. gobbara id. Tu. gobbara id.; ? kurpu id. Te. gobbaramu id.; (K also) gobbi a lump of cowdung worshipped as a goddess. Skt. go(r)vara- cowdung. Pkt, gov(v)ara- id. H. gobar fresh cowdung. Mar. govar Mar. govar dry cowdung. Turner, s.v. gobar.

Ta. kuppi vial, bottle. Ma. kuppi vial, bottle (chiefly of crystal). Ka. kuppi, kuppige vial, bottle. Kod. kuppi piece of glass, bottle. Tu. kuppi glass-ware, china-ware, bottle. Te. kuppe jar, bottle. Kui kupi an earthenware pot with a long, narrow neck and mouth, a goblet. /H. kuppi leather bottle for oil or ghee, vial. Turner, s.v. kuppā, kuppi.

Ta. kumpakāran potter. Ma. kumbhakaran id. To. kumo'rn id. Ka. kumbhakāra, kumbagāra, kumbāra, kumbara id. Kod. kumba:rë id.; stupid fellow. Tu. kumb e, kumbāre, kumbare potter Te. kumbhakārūdu, kummari id. Pa. kummal id. Go. (Muria, etc.) kummal id. Kui kumbarenju id.; fem. kumbareri. Kuwi (F) kümbra, (s) kumbra potter. /Skt. kumbhakāra potter. Pkt. kumbhaara-, kumbhara id. H. kumhār, Mar. kūbhär id. Turner, s. v. kumäle.
Ta. atti long pepper. Ma. atti elephant pepper. /? < Skt. hasti-pippali Scindapsus officinalis. Pkt. hatthi-pippali id.

Ta. kulam family, caste, genus, flock. Ma. kulam flock, family, Ko. kolm, golm caste, species, kind. To. kwasm genus (esp. of buffaloes); sacred name (of all things mentioned in prayers and songs); kwalm thing. Ka. kula herd, race, family, caste. Tu. kula family, race, tribe. Te. kulamu, kolamu caste, race, tribe, family, class. Kui klāmbu (pl. klāpka) family, lineage, kin, tribe, race, nationality, sort, species, variety, kind; kūlu family, clan, tribe, caste. Skt. kula- herd, race, family, caste.

Ta. kēţțai the 18th nakşatra; goddess of misfortune. Ma. kēțța the 18th lunar asterism. To, keot a heavenly body bringing misfortune. race. 26 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN 1 a Ka. jyēşthe, jēșțe, jēțe the 18th lunar mansion; goddess of misfortune. Tu. jyēșthe, jēştè misfortune, calamity. Te. jyėștha the 18th lunar mansion; elder sister of Lakshmi, the goddess of misfortune and poverty. /Skt. jyeșthā- the 18th lunar mansion; misfortune, personified as the elder sister of Lakşmi.

Ta. kēvu, kēvu, kērvu charge for transporting goods by sea, freight. Ma. kēvu, kēļi freight, passage money; kēvi shipper; kēļikka to freight. Tu. kēvu boat-hire. Te. kēvu freight. H. khewā ferryfare. Turner, s. v. khewāl (< Skt. kşepa-).

Ta. kēļi fun, jest, joke, ridicule, mimicry; kēļi, kēļikkai women's sport. Ma. kēli play, sport. Ko. geryļ, gey! sport, jest, amorous sport. To. ke‘ly mockery. Ka. gēli ridicule, derision. Tu. gēli ridicule, jest, mockery, insult. Te. gēli ridicule, mockery, joking. Skt. keliplay, sport, amorous sport, amusement. L. V.R. 1934. 263.
Ta. kottam costus root. Ma. koțțam Costus speciosus; Ocimum petiolare Rh. /Skt. kuştha- c. speciosus or arabicus. Pa. koţthaplant, ? c. speciosus. (C. speciosus Smith - C. arabicus Jacq.)

Ta. koțțāram granary, place where grains are husked, elephant stall, palace; koțțakāram, koțțu granary; koțțați storeroom, cattleshed. Ma. koțțāram, koțțakāram stable, place where temple affairs are managed, palace. Ka. koţțāra storeroom, treasury; koțāra threshing floor. Tu. koțţāra palace, storeroom. Te. koțțu, koțțați storehouse, shop; koțāramu, koțāru storehouse, magazine. Skt. koştha-, koșthāgāragranary, storeroom, treasury. Pkt. koţtha-, kotthā(g)āra-, koțțhāra- id. Mar, kothār granary; kothời storeroom.

Ta. kottamalli, kottamuri coriander, Coriandrum sativum. Ma. kottampalari id. Ka. kot(t)ambari, kot(t)umbari, kottiri, kottumari, kottumiri id. Tu. kottambari, kottamberi, kottembari, kottumbri id. Te. kot(t)imiri coriander plant or leaves. /Skt. kustumbari-, kustumburucoriander. Pkt. kutthumbhari- id:

Ta. kopparam elbow. Ka. koppara shoulder-blade. Te. kopparamu shoulder. Ga. (Oll.) kopre elbow. Skt. kūrpara- elbow. Pkt. koppara- id.

Ta. attuvānam ruins, desert, desolate place. Ma. addhvānam great exertion, fatigue; addhvāni diligent; addhvānikka to labor, work hard, exert oneself. Ka. adhvāna wilderness, forest, desert; misfortune; dearness, excess of price; (coll., L. V.R. 1934.255) immethodical, weak, bad, spoiled, useless. Tu. adhvana, advåna labor, immethodical effort; tired, weak, wrong, spoiled; addana weakness, sickness, affliction. Te. adhvānamu desolation, waste, ruin; adhvānapu desolate, waste, spoiled, bad, (B also) perplexing; adhvānamu cēyu to ruin, lay waste, spoil. /Skt. adhvan- (acc. adhvānam) road, journey, distance. L. V.R. 1934. 255-256. DICTIONARY 11 even-

Ka. golla, gollaļa cowherd. Kod. gollë man of cultivator caste. Tu. golle man of the cowherd or milkman caste. Te. golla caste of shepherds and herdsmen; a watchman, guard; gollāļu, gollavādu herdsman, shepherd; fem gollata, golladi. Mar. (Kulkarni) gol = gop cowherd. Cf. the various IA forms in Turner, s. v. gwālo.
Ga. (Oll.) göra horse. Go. kõļā id. Kui gõſa id. Kuwi (S) gõda id. Kur. ghoro id.; ghori mare. Malt. goro horse. /Skt. ghoțaka- horse. H. ghoſā, Mar. ghodā id. Turner, s.v. ghoſā.

Ta. kõți a score (as in counting precious stones, silk, etc.). Ma. kõți, kõțța Tu. köại id. Te. kõdiga id. (used chiefly in counting precious stones). Kui kõſie twenty. Kuwi (F) koreka, (S) kādi id. Kur, kuri Malt. kóși id. H. korī, Mar. kodi Turner, s.v. kori?.

Ta. kõtumai, kötumpai, koti wheat, Triticum vulgare. Ma. kõtampu, kõtampam. Ko. go dym, go dymb. To. kwï.Diby. Ka. godi, gödive, gödume, göduve. Ko. go.due (? go dve). Tu. godi, gödhi. Te. göd(h)uma. Kol. godma. Kol. godma. Nk. godma. Pa. gong. Go, gohk (pl.), (Pat.) gohku. Kui gohomo. Kui gohomo. Kuwi (S) gohonga. Kur. gohom. Malt. gohme. Br. khólum. Skt. godhūma- wheat. Pkt. gohūma- id. Bihari gohum, gohũ id. Turner, s.v. gahū.

Ta. komaram inspiration, possession by spirits. Ma. komaram oracle of a god, possessed devil-dancer. Skt. kumāra- boy, son, Skanda. Pkt. kumăra- id. The secondary derivative Skt. kaumāra-, Pkt. komāra- (also komara-), here means 'possessed by Skanda (Ta. murukan):
Ta. kõli jujube tree. Ma. kõlam jujuba. Ka. kola the fruit of jujube; kõli jujube tree, Zizyphus jujuba Lam. /Skt. koli- id.; kola- jujube fruit. C, J

Ta. akkulli, cakkulli a steamed meal-cake. Ka. cakkali, cakkuli, cakli, cakkuļi a ring of paste without sugar, but with a little salt, etc., fried in ghee or oil. Tu. cakkuli a cake made of rice flour, salt, etc., and fried in oil, Te. cakkilamu a kind of cake. Skt. śaskulĩ-, śaskulħa large round cake of ground rice, sugar, and sesamum, cooked in oil. Pkt. sakkuli- id. DED 2055 suggests with much uncertainty a Dravidian origin for the IA words. 28 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN 1 a
Ta, cakațu, cakațai, cākāțu, cāļu cart. Ma. cakațu, cāļu covered car. Ka. cak(k)adā, cakkadi cart. . Te. cekadā id. /Skt. śakața-, sakați- cart. Pkt. sagadi-, saada-, sāļi- id.

Ta. caki (-pp-, -tt-) to bear, tolerate, excuse, forgive; cakippu bearing, enduring, forgiving; cakippāļi one who bears with patience, one who forgives. Ma. sahikka to bear, endure, forgive. Ka. sahisu, sairisu, sayrisu to bear, bear patiently, suffer, endure, be patient, put up with, be able to bear up against; sairane, sayrane patience, endurance, bearing; sõsu to endure, bear. Tu. sahisuni, sayisuni to bear, endure, suffer, forgive; sairipuni, sairisuni to bear, endure, suffer; sairane patience, endurance. Te, saīcu to bear, endure, pardon, excuse, forgive; be agreeable, tasty (as food); saīpu, saſpudu, (K also) sayipu bearing, endurance; sairaņa patience, forgiveness; sairincu to be patient, endure, suffer, bear. /Skt. sah to bear, endure, tolerate, have patience with.

Ka. jagala a quarrel, fight, war. Kod. jagala a quarrel. Tu. jagaļa, jagaļāța, jaguļu quarrel, fight, dispute. Te. jagadamu a quarrel, dispute, fight, altercation, battle; vb. jagadam-āļu; jagașincu to quarrel, fight. Pkt. jhagada- quarrel. H. jhagrā id. Mar. jhagdā, jhagad id.; jhagadņē to quarrel. Turner, s. v. jhagaſă.

Ta. antastu rank, condition; story of a building. Ka. antastu being between; being one above another, tier, story of a building; degree of dignity, rank. Tu. antasty upper story or room; a secret. Te. antastu story of a house; arrangement of one above another; dignity, prestige. Skt. antaḥstha- being in the midst or between. L. V.R. 1934.257.

Ta. cankațam ferryboat of two canoes with a platform thereon (said to be < Ptg. jangada); cankāļam a kind of boat; cankuvațam ferryboat (said to be < Ptg. jangada). Ma. cannātam ferryboat, made of two boats. Ka. jangāl platform on two boats, used at ferries. Tu. jangălų, jangāru wooden platform placed on boats. Skt. samghāța- joining of timber. Pa. sanghāța- union, raft. Pkt. samghāda- pair, couple. Mar. săgad double-canoe. Sgh. hanguļuva, aŭguļa id. Turner, s.v. sanāri. Periplus váyyapov. Ptg. jangada, for which see Dalgado-Soares, Portuguese Vocables in Asiatic Languages. Also see Hobson-Jobson, s. w. jancada, jangar.

Ta. cañkili chain, link, fetter. Ma. cannala chain; cannu small chain to which to hang keys. Ko. caŋgyl chain; tega'l, tega lg door-chain. To. tagas chain (in poetry: ka(s) tegas stone chain (in the story of chaining the sun); pï(n) tegas gold chain); tokwal leg chains (of elephant; in poetry); prison, sentence to prison. Ka. śşńkhala, śộnkhale, sankale, sańkole iron chain, any chain or fetter; chain for confining the feet of an elephant. Kod. caŋŋo•le chain. Tu. sankale, sankõlè id., fetter. Te. sankela id. Kol. sakri chain. Pa. cakril id. Go. (W) sánkar id. Kui sikal, sikali id. Kuwi (F) hikri, (S) hikni, hikli id. /Skt. śřńkhală - chain. Pkt. sank(h)ală- id. H. sãkal, sãkar, sãkrī, sīkar, sikal. Turner, s.v. sānlo. a DICTIONARY 29

Ka. sajjige, sajjaka, sojjige, sõji wheaten flour in fine granules, wheaten grits, rolong; grits of roasted rice, a mess or dish made of grits of roasted rice. Tu. sajjige, sojjigè, sõji rolong or wheaten grits. Te. sojje, (B also) sojji rice boiled after being roasted. /H. Mar. soji id. Turner, s.v. suji.

Ka. saņal(u), saņil(u), sadlu to become loose, become slack, relax, become lax; caus. sadalisu, saờilisu, sadilcu, sadlisu; sad(a)la, sad(a)lu, sadila, saờilu, salla, sallu the state of being loose, slack, relaxed, or lax. Kod. sadala looseness. Tu. sadily loose, slack, loosened. Te. sadalu to become loose or slack, be loosened; n. looseness, slackness; sadalincu, sadal(u)cu to loosen, untie. /Pkt. sadhila-, siļhilaloose (cf. Skt. śithila- id.). Cf. Burrow, The Sanskrit Language 45 f. Cf. entry 183, Ka. dilla.

Ka. jadi, jidi a long-continued, fine, small rain. Tu. jadipini, jadipuni, jadiyuni to rain incessantly. Te. jadi rain. Malt. jara rain. | Pkt. jhadi- continuous rain (DNM). Mar. jhaời long-continued rain. H. jhaf heavy shower. Turner, s.v. jhari.

Ta. caņți wicked man or woman; obstinate, perverse person. Ma. canți obstinate, stubborn. Ko. candy man who will not listen to advice. Ka. candi an obstinate man; obstinacy. Tu. canda vehemence, obstinacy; vehement, obstinate, quarrelsome. Te, caņdi obstinate, stubborn; an obstinate person. /Skt. canda- fierce, violent, cruel, passionate.

Ka. sanna, sanna small, tiny, thin, delicate, slender; smallness, etc. Kod. canna, sanna small. Te. sanna, sannani, sannamu thin, slender, narrow, fine, gentle, not loud; sannana thinness, smallness, narrowness, fineness. Skt. ślakṣṇa- slippery, smooth, tender, small. Pkt. sanha-, sanha smooth, small. Turner, s.v. sānu.
Ta. caturam square; caturi (-pp-, -tt-) to cut or make a square figure. Ma. caturam square. Ko. cadrm (obl. cadrt-) a square, a Te, cadaramu square (n. and adj.). Skt. catur- four.

Ta. canti joint, etc.; cantu joint, hips, road-crossing, narrow street, lane, gap, crack, cleft. Ma. cantu joint, cleft; sandhu joint, limb; canti buttocks, posteriors; sandhi union, joint, vulva. Ko. cand joint; narrow path between houses. To. sod joint. Ka. sandhi, sandi cross. 30 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN joint, etc.; sandu juncture, joint, lane, cleft, fissure. Kod. candi anus; vulva. Tu. sandhi union, juncture, etc.; sandy, sandu cleft, joint. Te. sandu narrow street, lane, corner, opening, fissure, crack, hole. Skt. samdhi- junction, joint, interstice, crevice, vulva. L. V.R. 1935, 74.

Ta. anti twilight, morning and evening prayers. Ma. anti ing. Ko. ande:l time after sunset until about 9 P. M.; ande:l poſt afternoon from about 4 to 6 P. M.; inde:l this last night, yesterday night; this coming evening. Koạ. andi evening just after dark; andi-kotti evening star in west. Skt. samdhi- interval between day and night, twilight.

Ta. cantai a fair, market, Shandy, bazaar, multitude. Ma. canta a fair, weekly or annual market. Ko. caynt market. To. soty market day; week. Ka. sante, santi assemblage, fair or market, market-place. Kod. catte market. Tu. santé id., fair. Konda sata village market. Skt. samsthā- assembly (lex.; but cf. BHS samsthāgāra-, Pa. samthāgāraassembly hall); Pkt. *samthă-. Cf. also Skt. samsthāna- public place in a town, Pa. saņthāna- meeting place, market. The etymology usually given is Skt. samdhā-, which does not have the meaning 'assembly' (though samdhāna- does).

Ta. capparam canopied vehicle or small car on wheels in which idols are carried during festivals, testered bedstead. Ma. capparam shed or thatch, litter of an idol and place where it is kept. To. soporm shed. Ka. cappara frame thrown over houses to form the roof, shed, thatched or tiled roof, canopy of a bedstead. Tu. cappara shed, pandal. Te. capparamu canopied seat in which an idol is carried about, shed or pandal, canopy of a bed. (H. chappar thatched roof, hut (< Skt. chattvarahouse, bower). Turner, s.v. chāpro.

Ta. campaļam provisions for journey; wages, salary. Ma. campa- ļam, śampalam wages, salary. wages, salary. Ko. cambaļm id. To. sobulm id. Ka. sambaļa provender for journey; pay, salary (monthly or yearly). Tu. sambala pay, salary, wages. Te. sambalamu, sambalamu, sambadamu id. /Skt. sambala- provisions for a journey. Turner, s.v. sāmal.

Ta. campaļi betel pouch, bag, wallet. Ka. sambalige a covered box made of õle. Te. sambaļika, sambela wallet, satchel, esp. for holding betel leaves, nuts, etc. Skt. sampuța(ka)-, sampuţikā- box, casket.
Kod. jams- (jamsi -) to utter (incantation). Tu. jamipuni id. Skt. jalp- to mutter, say. Pkt. jamp- id.

Ta. carākai metal cup (loc.); caruvam shallow, wide-mouthed vessel. To. tarx bronze food vessel. Ka. caravige, carivige, carvige, а 1 DICTIONARY 31 cavarige, cavurige a large copper or brass pot in the form of a cambu for carrying water; carige, cerige id.; (= cambu) a globular copper or glass vessel, used for drinking water. Tu. carige a cooking utensil of copper or brass. Te. cerava, ceravamu a brass kettle or boiler. Skt. saraka- drinking vessel; sarāva(ka)- shallow cup, plate, platter; there seems to have been contamination or development of meaning.

Ta. cari similarity, suitability, agreement, exactness, rightness, propriety, regularity, equal measure or quantity; yes, right. Ma. sari, sari even, like, equal, right, correct. Ko. cery equal, good, right, correct; cerya'n excellent, beautiful, clever, very. To. sary right, correct; height. Ka. sari the state or condition of being adjusted, fitness, propriety, suitableness, rightness, correctness, evenness, sameness, similarity, equality, an equal thing, fit, proper, right, reasonable; vb. to put in proper order, adjust; sarikatana equality of position; sariga an equal, a man of equal power; saru sameness, equality. Kod. sëri correct. Tu. sari equal, like; just, right, proper, fit, even, not odd, full; interj. very good; sarike right, fit, proper, level, even, abundant, complete; sarta straight, direct; sarāriyuni to be exact; sarāsari equally, alike, right, proper, on average. Te. sari equal, equivalent, suitable, fit, proper, corresponding, similar, like, just like, reasonable, correct, right, faultless, straight, level, even, flat, not odd, completed, equality, similarity, etc.; yes, all right; (K also) sar(u)du, sarusu to distribute equally, (coll.) economize. Kui sarna straight, outstretched, upright. Kur. to put in its proper place, stow. Malt. saryare to be cured, be ready; saryatre to cure, mend, correct. Br. ? shar good, beautiful; well, properly (also Bal.). Skt. sadṛśa- like, resembling, suitable, fit. Pkt. sari- id.

Ka. cala dazzle; caļacaļa, calacaļane dazzlingly; jalakkane, jalarkane, jalak(k)ane clearly, purely, brightly, shiningly; clearness, etc. Tu. caļacaļa glittering; jalujaly brightly; jalakų glitter, gleam; jalakuni to shine; jalakāvuni to cause to shine. /Mar. jha!ak, jhaljha! glitter. Turner, s. vv. jhalak, jhalkanu, jhaljhal.

Ta. callā muslin; cēlai cloth, saree. Ma. sallāvu muslin; callā cloth without a border, as muslin; cēla cloth, esp. of women. Ka. śalya, śalle muslin cloth without a border; cēla, salya, śalle, selle, śēle, sēle cloth, clothes, garment. Kod. ce le belt, sash worn by Kodagu man. Tu. śalya, śallè, sēlè, cēlè a thin upper cloth, generally without border. Te. sellä a cloth without a border; cēla, cēlamu cloth, clothing. Skt. cela clothes, garment. Mar. sela a sort of robe. Cf.
