Ta. appatſam unmixed, pure. Ka. appața id. Te. appațamu id., unadulterated. Skt. asprsta- untouched. But the MIA forms of Skt. sprś- have u in general.

Ta. calli short pendant in ornaments, hangings. Ka. jalli, jhalli tassels, hangings, a whisk made of the tail of the camara. chaplet of flowers, flowers dangling down the head, etc., anything dangling or hanging loosely. Te. jalli a whisk, tassel. [Cf. Mar. jhālar, jhallar fringe, etc.; jhāl tassel; jhaļam that hangs dangling and waving in the wind. Turner, s. v. jhālar.
Ka. jalli, jalle large round bamboo basket used for storing corn. Te. jalla a long narrow basket placed on a cart for carrying grain. /H. jhāl, jhalla, jhalli large basket. Turner, s.v. jhālar.

Ta. calli falsehood (< Te.); callikkaran liar, hypocrite. Ka. jalli falsehood, a lie; jala fraud, hypocrisy; jalika a deceiver. Tu. jalli boast, bragging; jalliyuni to boast, brag. Te. jalli falsehood, false; jallikādu a liar. H. ja'i forgery; jaʻli forged, counterfeit, false, spurious (< Ar.).

Ta. cavaļam bearded dart or lance, pike. Ma. cavalam lance, a bearded javelin. Ka. sabaļa spear, lance, pike (one of the tatsamas). Te. sabalamu a kind of spear. /Skt. sarvalā-, śarvala an iron club or crowbar. Pkt. savvala-, sabbala- spear. Turner, s. v. såbal.

Ta. cavu (-pp-, -tt-) to fall in price, become cheap, be unsaleable, have no demand; cavukkai cheapness; cavutam id., old stock of goods lying unsold. Ka. cavuka cheap. Te, cavuka, cauka cheapness; cheap. /Mar. savãg cheap; savõgņē to become cheap (< Skt. samarghacheap; Turner, s.v. sahango).

Ta. cavukkam square piece of cloth, towel. Ka. cavuka, cauka, cauku a small uncolored square handkerchief. Kod. cavka long white headdress worn by women at funeral; the modern long headdress of women. Te. caukamu a square, a towel that is square. Skt. catuṣka consisting of four, square. Pkt. caükka- id. Turner, S. v. cok.

Ka. jāyi, jāji, jādi, jā mace, nutmeg (Myristica moschata Thunb.); Jasminum grandiflorum Lin. Tu. jāji J. grandiflorum; jāji-kāyi -the nutmeg. Te. jāji, jādi id. Skt. jāti- mace, nutmeg; J. grandiflorum. Pkt. *jādi-, jāi- id. (M. fragrans Houtt. M. moschata Thunb. Native to the Eastern Moluccas.)

Ta. căți (-pp-, -tt-) to slander; chide, reprove; n. malicious report, slander; câțu (cāți- ) to abuse, reprove. Ka. câţi, câda, cahada slander; cāda slanderer; fem, cāļi; jādisu . to reprove. Kod. ca di talebearing, information laid against someone. Tu. cāļi slander; cāļiyuni to slander. Te. cāļĩ backbiting. /Mar. cahāļ, cāļ a traducer, defamer; cahādi, cāļi defamation, slander.

Ta. cāļi jar, a measure of capacity. Ma. câți jar. Ko. cairy : 1 1 DICTIONARY 33 Tu. prabig basket with wide mouth. To. toʻſy, to·dy broad storage basket. Ka. jādi jar. Tu. jāļi large earthen vessel. Te. jāņi large bottle or jar. /Pa. cāți- jar, waterpot. H. cāți earthen vessel or pitcher. The forms with j- may result from contamination with forms of the H. Mar. group jhāri water-pot with spout; cf. Turner, s.v. jhāri?.
Ta. cāņakam, cānam, cāņi cowdung. Ma. cāņakam, cānam, cāņi id. Kod. caiņa id. Skt. chagana- dried cowdung. dried cowdung. Pkt. chagana-, *chaaņa-, chāna- id. Mayrhofer, s. v. chaganaḥ.

Ta. appaņai command. Ka. appane order, command, law; permission, leave. Kod. appaņe order. Tu. appaņè command, order; permission, leave. Te. appaņa, appana id. Skt. ājñāpana- ordering (so Ta. Lex., Kitt.). ? Skt. arpaņa- consigning, entrusting; Pkt. appaņaid.

Ta. cāņai, cāņai-kkal grindstone, whetstone. Ma. cāņa id. Ko. ca'n sharpness (of razor, knife), smoothness (of ground spice); ca'n kal whetstone. Ka. sāņe, sāņe-kal grindstone, whetstone. Tu. sāņè, sāņekallu id. Te. sāna id. Skt. śāņa- whetstone, grindstone.

Ta. catam boiled rice; căppiţu (căppițuv-, cāppiţt-) to eat, drink, consume, misappropriate; căppățu food, meal (esp. of human beings); cāppăţțu-rāman glutton. Ma. śāppāțu a meal of brahmans. sādamu cooked rice. Te. sadamu food, rice; pasādamu, (K also) pasadanamu boiled rice, cooked food; pasāpadu to eat; sāpaļu to eat, , dine; sāpāțu a meal, food. /Skt. prasāda- food presented to god or guru. L. V. Ramaswami Aiyar, IHQ 12.265-6 (also L. V.R. 1935. 67).

Ta. cámi lord, the Supreme Being, chieftain, master, guru, a term of respectful address; cuvāmi id. Ma. sāmi, svāmi id. Ko. co‘ym god. Ka. sāmi, sāyi, sāvi, somi, sõyi, svāmi id. Tu. Sāmi, svāmi id. Te. sāmi, svāmi id. /Skt. svāmin- id. (not the Supreme Being). Pkt. sāmi- id.

Ta. camai common millet, Panicum miliaceum; poor man's millet, P. crusgalli; little millet, P. miliare. Ma. cāma P. miliaceum. Ko. ta'ym millet; ta'ym gu', ta'm gu' cooked millet (ku: cooked rice). To. ta'm ašky husked millet (ašky husked grain, rice). Ka. sāme, save P. frumentaceum. Tu. sāmè millet, P. miliaceum. Te. (K) cama id. Pa. cāma small grain (Halbi gaţkā). Skt. śyāmăka- P. frumentaceum. Pkt. samăa- id. H. sämā, sāwā, săwă id. Mar. sãvā, sāvā id. Turner, s.v. samā?. (P. crus-galli Linn.; P. c., var, frumentaceum - P. frumentaceum Roxb. P. miliaceum Linn. and P. miliare Lamk. have synonymies that "are almost inextricably mixed.")

Ta. сārāyam spirituous liquor, arrack. Ma. сārāyam distilled liquor, wine. To. so'roy spirituous liquor. Ka. sărāya, sărāyi id., arrack. Tu. sārāyi id. Te. sārāya, sārā id. id. Skt. sara essence, nectar.

Ta. ālai apartment, hall, elephant stall or stable; cālai sacrificial or alms hall, school, stable, cow shed, house. Ma. āla shed, work- 34 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN COWshop, cowhouse; śāla hall, house, stable; cāla palace. Ko, a:l shed. To. a's Toda house. Ka. sālā, sāle, sāli, śāle hall, room; school. Tu. sāle, śāle id. Te. sāla house, shed, pandal, hall. Pa. cēla shed. Kuwi (S) hā'la stable, stall, workshop. Skt. śālā- house, hall, shed, stable. Pkt. sālā id. H. sāl house, hall, school. Mar. sāļ workshop. Turner, s.v. -sär3.

Te. jāva gruel, porridge. Pa. cava rice gruel; vār jāva water in which rice has been boiled (cf. DED 4387). Go. jawā porridge, gruel of kõdon and kuțkī; (Pat.) jāwa rice gruel; (W) jáwá penjh (cooked food); (L) jāvā porridge; jāvānā to eat porridge. Konda jāva cooked rice. Kui (P) jau dhal, gravy, soup. /Skt. yavagu- rice-gruel. BHS yvägl-, yāgu- id. Pa. yāgu- id. Turner, s.v. jāulo, esp. Or. jāu overboiled rice, etc.
Ta. cicam lead; iyam white lead, black-lead. Ma. iyam lead. Ko. ti.cl id.; ti cay tin. To. ti'sïl id. Ka. sisa, sisu lead. Tu. sisa id. Te. sisamu id. /Skt. sisa- lead.

Ta. cirakam cumin, Cuminum cyminum. Ma. cirakam id. Ка. jiraka, jīrage, jirige, jīrā id. Tu. jīradari, jīrige id. Te. jirakamu, jīraṇamu, jīlakar(r)a id. Skt. jiraka-, jirana- id. Pkt. jīraa- id. H. jirā id. Turner, s. v. jiro.

Ta, curikai short sword, knife; cūri, cūri-kkatti a kind of sharp knife. Ma. curika dagger, small sword; cūri dagger, knife in a walking stick. Ko, cu'ry flensing knife, two-edged knife. To. tu'ry knife (any kind except billhook). Ka. surige, surigi, suragi knife, dagger; cūri small billhook-like knife. Tu. suriya a demon's straight sword; cūri knife, small sword. Te. suriya, sure knife; cūri, cũra-katti knife. Skt. kşura- razor; kşurikā- knife; chữrikā-, chữri- knife. Pkt. chura-, churi(g)ā-, churi- id. Turner, s. v. churi and App.
Ta. amayam, amaiyam opportunity, occasion. fit or convenient time, opportunity, festive occasion, season. /Skt. samayaopportunity, occasion, season.

Ta. cul littleness, smallness, slenderness; culļalan thin slender man; fem. cullali; culli smallness. Ma. cullu what is little, trifling. /Skt. kşulla- small, minute. Pkt. chulla id. However, there is also Pa. Pkt. culla- id.; see Turner, s.v. chulyāhā.

Ta. cūci, ūci needle. Ma. sūci, tūśi id., iron style. Ko. tu'c needle. Ka. sūci, śūci, sūji, sūje id. Kod. cu di id. Tu. dūji, sūji id., pin. Te. sūci, sūcika, sūdi needle. Kol. su:di id. Nk. sūdi id. Pa. cūcub id. Ga. (Oll.) suja (j = z) id. Konda sūzi id. Kui susi id. Kuwi (F) sūja, (S) sūza (z = j) id. Kur, suſtu, suytu pointed; suyu pointed-nosed; suwa packing-needle. Malt. cúci pointed, sharp. Skt. sūc- needle. Pkt. sui- id. H. sui needle; sūjā packing-needle, awl; sūji needle, small awl. Turner, s. vv. siyo?, sujā. DICTIONARY 35 a

Ta. cūtu gambling. Ma. cūtu id. Ko. cu'jm (obl. cu'jt - ) bet, a race. To. twï'zm (obl. twï.zt-) a bet. Ka. jūdu, jūja, jūju, dyūta gambling. Kod. ju'ji a bet. Tu. jūji, jūju gaming, a wager. Te. . jūjamu, jūdamu gambling. /Skt. dyūta- gambling. Pa. jūta- id. Pkt. *jūda-, jūa- id. Turner, S. v. juwa?.
Ta. cekku oilpress; cekkān, cekkāțti worker of oilpress. Ma. cekkan oilmaker. Ka. cekku oilpress, sugar mill. /Skt. cakra wheel; oil-mill. Pkt. cakka id. Turner, s. v. cāko.
Ka. cejje, cajje, sejje, sajje place of rest or repose, bed. Te. sejja bed, couch. Skt. sayya- bed. Pa. seyyā id. Pkt. sejjā- id. H. sej id.

Ta. cețți vaiśya or mercantile caste, title of traders; fem. cețțicci; cețțimai, ceļļu trade, traffic; etti title of distinction conferred on persons of the Vaiśya caste, the Vaisya caste. Ma. cețți, cettiyan, ettiyān one of the foreign merchant classes; fem. cetticci; cettu trade. To. sity man of Chetti caste (Tamilian). Ka. sețți, sațți, cațți a banker, merchant or tradesman. Te. setti merchant. Skt. śreșthin person of authority, head of a guild. Pa. Pkt. setthi- id., merchant. Cf. H. seth, Guj. śeth head of a guild, banker. Turner, s.v. seth?.
Ta. cețți wrestler, prizefighter. Ka. jețţi, jețtiga, jațți, jattiga professional wrestler. Tu. jețți wrestler. / Mar. jethi id. (< Skt. jyestha-).

Ta. contam one's own peculiar right, exclusive property, near relationship; contakkāran owner, close relation. Ma. Sontam Ko. condm (obl. condt-) close relationship, ownership; one's own; condka.rn, condga'rn owner, close relation. Ka. sonta, svanta belonging to oneself; state of being one's own. Tu. sonta, svanta Те. sontamu own, private. /Skt. sva one's own. Cf. also Pa., BHS santaka- belonging to; ? contamination. S. Anavaratavinayakam Pillai, Dravidic Studies III. 46f., gives other variations and suggests svatantraas the origin; the meaning of the latter is not close, but again contamination is a possibility.

Ka. jompa, jompe cluster, bunch, a mass. Te. jompamu thick foliage, a cluster of leaves, flowers and branches. Pa. joppa bunch, cluster. Kur. jhopā cluster or bunch (fruit, flowers, etc.), ball of thread. Malt. jopa, jopeli bunch, cluster. / H. jhõpā bunch, cluster. Turner, s. v. jhuppo.

Ta. cóți, cāļu a pair, similarity; cõți (-pp-, -tt-) to arrange, adorn. Ma. jõțu, cóțu a pair. Ko. jo'ry id. ; jo'șc- (jo rc-) to put on (jewelry). To. twï'ſ, swi'd a pair. Ka. jõdu, joļi union, a pair, equality, own. own. 36 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN sameness; jõạisu to join, unite; collect; assemble; get ready. Kod. jo:ļi pair. Tu. joļi, jāļu pair; equal, like; jodiyuni to be joined; jõdipuni to join, unite. Te. jõdu, jāņā pair; equal; jödincu to join, unite. Kol. jodi pair. Pa. jorto join, mix together. Kui jõſe pair. Kur. joſā id.; jõộnā to unite or join to, put into shape. Malt. jóra pair; jóſare to be united, copulate; joratre, jórye to unite, couple. Br. joſa pair, match; jõſa kanning to put in. (H. jor union, pair; joſi pair, equal; jornā to join, unite, tie, collect, etc. Mar. jodnē id.; jod, joļi pair, etc. Turner, S. vv. jor?, jornu, jurnu.

Ma. amparam, amparam hog-plum, wild mango, Spondias mangifera. Ka. amațe, ambațe, ambața, ambāde, avaje id. Tu. ambațe, ambaờè id. Skt. ambarișa-, amlavāțaka-, ämravățaka-, āmrātaka- id. Pa. ambāțaka id. Pkt. ambāda(g)a- id. H. ābārā, Mar. ābādā id. Turner, S. V. amaro.

Ta. cöti (-pp-, -tt-) to search, investigate, examine, test, cleanse. Ma. sõdhikka, cödikka, cötikka to search, question. Ko. co.dc- (co'dc-) to examine, test. Ka. sõdisu to search, examine. Kod. co dïi n. taste; co'dï no‘t- to taste (no:ț- to look at). Tu. śödhipuni, śõdhiyuni, sodiyuni to search, examine, try, assay. Te, sõdincu to search, examine; ? sõdi, sõde fortune-telling by a gypsy woman. /Skt. śudh-, caus. śodhay- to put to test, try, examine.

Ta. ñāyam, nāyam, niyāyam justice, law, argument, debate, usage. Ma. ñāyam reason, right, complaint, custom. Ko. na‘ym (obl. na'yt-) justice, decision, dispute; na'ymgaörn headman. To. no'ym (obl. no'yt-) dispute, the tribal council. Ka. nyāya, nāya, nėya right, justice, argument, dispute, quarrel, lawsuit, judgment. Koș. ne ya”, (in song) ña'ya" dispute. Tu, nyāya, nāya justice, law, quarrel; right, just. Te. nyāyamu, nāyamu, nėyamu method, justice; just. Skt. nyāyamethod, fitness, lawsuit, judgment, argument. Pa. ñāya- id. Pkt. ņāya-, nāya- id. D

Ka. dilla, dilla unnerved, tottering state, agitation of mind, fear; șillisu to totter, become agitated. Tu. dily, ļīla, dīlu loose, unrestrained. Te. Pillamu stupefaction, weariness, weakness; dilla-padu DICTIONARY 37 to be astounded, stupefied, unnerved, be wearied; dīlu loose, lean, thin, weak; to become loose; dilā weakness; weak; dīlu weariness, thinness, looseness; wearied, weak; to grow tired or weak. /Mar. Ņhilā loose, slack; dhillī slackness; dhīl id.; loose, slack. H. dhīlā loose, weak. Turner, s.v. Ņhilo: Pkt. Ņhilla-, connection improbable with Pkt. sadhila-, sidhila- (cf. entry 133, Ka. sadal(u)); contra Pischel $150.

Te. dokka hard covering of a nut, etc., shell. Pa. (S) doki tortoise shell. Go. (Koya) dok shell (of tortoise, egg). Kui ļāki skull, shell (of tortoise, turtle, coconut, egg). /Mar. doki, dokē the head. Turner, s.v. doko. T, D

Ta. takku dodge, trick. Ka. takk, bikki fraud, dishonest doings. Te. takku to pretend, feign; n. pretending, pretense. Mar. thakņē to be deceived; thak, ţhag a knave, rogue. Turner, s.v. țhag, țhagnu.

Ta. tanțam staff, stick, branch of tree, club, pestle, punishment, penalty, loss, army; tanțu staff, stick, branch tree, club, pestle, bridge of nose, army; tanți (-pp-, -tt-) to punish. Ma. tanțu stick, staff, pole for bearing a burden, oar; daņdam stick, staff, punishment, army; dandikka to punish. Ko. taņd handle of broom, bridge of nose; tadm (obl. tadt-) a fine; dand punishment, fine; fight, marauding; daņạm (obl. dandt-) loss; dandc- (dandc-) to punish. To, todm fine paid to members of assembly belonging to opposite sub-caste, for contempt of assembly; tod army. Ka. tandu staff, club, heavy (iron) club; danda stick, staff, cudgel, oar, punishment, fine, army; dandisu to punish; danļu army. Koď. tanại big stick. Tu. dantè walking stick, staff; dandu oar; army; danda staff, stick, punishment, loss; daņdipuni, dandisuni to punish. Te. daņdamu rod, stick, staff, punishment, army, collection; dandincu to punish; dandu army, multitude; danļūdu Yama; danduga, danduva, daņduvu an extortion, fine, loss. / Skt. danda- stick, staff, club, sceptre as a symbol of power, violence, army, punishment, fine. Cf. also L. V. R. 1935. 64. Cf. also DED 2479, for items about which there is uncertainty whether they are borrowed from Skt. or are originally Dravidian.

Ta. tanțai trouble, vexation; tanță id., dispute, squabble. Ka. . tanțe quarrel, dispute, trouble, annoyance. Koď. tanțe trouble, annoy- Tu. tante id., meddling. Te. tanța, tanțā difficulty, trouble, dispute, slander. H. tāță, țățā wrangling, noisy quarrel. Mar. tātā ance. 38 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN worm. quarrel, a troublesome business. The Skt. root tand- to beat, which is compared by Kulkarni, is found in the Dhātupātha only.

Ta. tattu blotch, slight swelling as from the bite of an insect K Te.). Ka. taddu, daddu rash, herpes; ringworm. Tu. taddu an eruption or swelling, erysipelas; daddu ringworm, herpes. Te. daddu, dadduru herpes; a slight swelling of the skin, as from the bite of an insect. Pa. dad ringworm. Kui dado, dadu rough white patches on the skin that cause irritation and itching, dry itch. Kuwi (F) tadū ring- Kur. daddū id. /Skt. dadrŭ-, dardū cutaneous eruption, kind of leprosy. Pa. Pkt. daddu- id. H. dad ringworm, herpes, shingles. Turner, s.v. dād. Mayrhofer, s.v. dadrúh.

Ta. tapalai a kind of metal vessel; tavalai metallic pot with a wide mouth. Ma. tavala, takala a small cooking vessel of brass. Ko. tapa'l metal water-vessel. Ka. tapale, tappale, tapēli a round brass or copper cooking vessel. Tu. tapalè a large metallic cooking vessel, saucepan. Te. tapēla a small or portable vessel of any metal. Mar. tapelē, tapeli a culinary utensil (said to be a derivative of Skt. tap- to be hot); tavli a metal or earthen vessel.
Ta. arankam island formed by a river or rivers, delta. Te. lanka island, islet. (Cf. Skt. lankā-.
Ta. tappaņam tacking needle. Ka. dabbana, dabbaļa pack-needle. Tu. dabbana bodkin, large packing needle. Te. dabbanamu id. Mar. dābhan pack-needle.

Ta. tampalam red spittle caused by chewing betel, refuse of chewed betel. Te, tamma, (K also) tammalamu chewed mass or lump of betel leaves and areca nuts. /Skt. tāmbūla- betel leaf. Pkt. tambolaid. H. tābol id. Turner, s. v. tamol.

Ta. tarukkam, tarkkam reasoning, arguing, discussion, dispute; tarukku disputation; takkam dispute, objection. dispute, objection. Ma. tarkam reasoning, dispute. Ka. tarka Ka. tarka id., discussion. Kod. takki talk, words; language. Tu. tarka dispute, discussion. Te. tarkamu reasoning, discussion. /Skt. tarka- reasoning, confutation. Pkt. takka id.

Ta. taruppai, tarppai the sacred grass, Poa cynosuroides. Ko. dab, da(b) pul grass, Andropogon schoenanthus. Ka. darbha, darbhe, darbe, dabbe P. cynosuroides. Tu. darbhè, darbe id. Te. darbha id. /Skt. darbha- bunch of grass. Pkt. dabbha id. (Eragrostis cynosuroides Beauv. - Poa cynosuroides Retz. A. s. is a different species.)

Ta. tavacam grain, esp. dry. Ko. davcm (obl. davct-) grain in general. Ka. tavasa, davasa corn, grain. Tu. davasa produce of the field, grain in general. Te. (B) davasamu grain. /Skt. yavasa- grass, fodder. Pkt. javasa- id.

Ta. talam thickness as of a board, heaviness. Ka. daļa thick- DICTIONARY 39 ness, stoutness, solidness. Tu. daļa thick, stout, robust. Te. daļamu id., much, great; thickness. Skt. drịha- firm, hard, strong, solid, massive; dşdham firmly, thoroughly, much. Pkt. dadha - Skt. drờha-. Turner, s. v. daro (esp. Sgh. daļa hard).

Ta. talam army. Ma. talam, dalam id.; daļavāyi a general. Ka. dara, daļa army; daravāyi a general. Kod. daļaba'y id. Tu. dala, daļavāda army; daļavāyi general of an army. Te. daļamu, daļamu army; daļavāyi general. /Skt. dala a detachment of troops. H. dal, Mar. dal army. Turner, s. v. dal.

Ko. talm (obl. talt-) palm of hand. Ka. tala, tala level surface; palm of the hand, sole of the foot; lower part, base, bottom (taļa is one of the tatsamas). Tu. tala, tala base, bottom. Te. talamu id., surface, palm of hand, sole of foot. Kuwi (F) talepau sole of foot. /Skt. talasurface, base, palm of hand, sole of foot.

Ta. tali temple, sacred shrine, place, room. Ma. taļi temple, holy building, asylum, assembly hall. Ka. tali fence, place of refuge, asylum, a covert, choultry for travellers, the building appointed for the distribution of food to brahmans, etc. /Skt. sthalī- place, spot. Pkt. thali- id.

Ta. talikai eating-plate, platter. Ma. talika metal plate turned up at the rim, plate to measure out boiled rice in temples. Ka. talige, tanige a metal plate turned up at the rim. Kod. talia plate. Te. taliga, taliya a dish for rice used in a Vaishnava temple. Skt. sthālavessel, plate, cup, bowl, pot; sthālī- earthen dish or pan, cooking vessel. BHS sthālaka-, sthālikā- pot. Pa. thālaka-, thālikā - id. Pkt. thalliāearthen dish. H. thaliyā plate, dish, platter. Cf. DED 2600.

Ta. aran, aranam defence, fortress; araņi (-pp-, -tt-) to fortify, defend; araņiya adj. defended; araṇ-manai royal palace, mansion. Ma. aran stronghold; araṇippu being impregnable. /Skt. śaraṇa- shelter. Skt. arana- refuge < Dr.

Ta, akankāram conception of individuality, arrogance, haughtiness; änkāram id., kindness, love; ānkāri (-pp-, -tt-) to be arrogant, insolent. Ma. ahankāram, ānkāram feeling of self, pride, self-conceit, boisterousness. Ko. a'ŋkarm (obl. a.şka'rt-) joyful pride, joyfulness. Ka. ahamkāra concept of individuality, pride; ahamkarisu to be proud. Tu. ahankāra, ānkāra self-consciousness, pride, haughtiness; ahankaripuni, ankariyuni to be proud, arrogant. Te. ahankāramu, (K also) ãkaramu egotism, pride, arrogance; ahankarincu to be arrogant. Skt. ahamkāra- conception of one's individuality, pride, haughtiness.
Ta, tarai land, ground; tarai id., the earth. Ma. tara ground, mound, elevated ground. Skt. dharā- the earth.

Ta. tācari, tācan Vaišnava non-brahmin mendicant; tācari-ppāmpu hermit snake, large rock snake, as having an upright white streak like the forehead mark of a tācari. Ko. da'cn n. pr. bullock with white star on forehead; fem. da'c ( da c-y); da.cn man who begs from house to house; n. pr. man whose father begged thus to get the people's blessings when he had no son. Ka. dāsa, dāsara, dāsari servant; Vaishṇava religious mendicant; dāsa-hāvu, dāsara-hāvu, dāsari-hāvu boa (said to be called so because it has an upright white line on the forehead, or because marked with white streaks, like Vaishnavas). Te. dasari Vaishnava mendicant of the Sudra class; dāsari-pāmu a kind of snake. Skt. dāsaservant.

Ta. tāci, tāti maidservant; dancing girl, harlot. To, to Oy maid- 40 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN Ko. ta'ſ ness. servant. Ka. dāsi id.; harlot. Tu. dāsi maidservant. Te. dási id.; dancing girl. Kuwi (S) dáseni dancing girl. /Skt. dāsi- female servant, harlot.

Ta. tāți chin, beard, dewlap, hanging excrescence under a cock's neck; tāțai cheeks, chaps, jawbone; tāpjaws, adam's apple; tavațai cheek. Ma. tāți jawbone, chin, beard; tāța dewlap of a bull. (obl. ta't-) cheek just beside mouth. Ka. dāļi beard; dāde tusk, fang, jawbone; davaṣe jawbone. Kod. ta'ời beard; ta'ời kuțți, (Mercara) ta di kokki chin; davade chin; davade cheek. Tu, dādè tusk, fang; dāļi beard; davadè jaw, cheek. Te. davuda id. Go. tādwă chin. Skt. dāhā- tusk; dādhikabeard; tusk. Pkt. dadha- tusk; dādhia- beard, chin. H. dāșhā fang; dāșhi beard. Turner, s. v. dāro, dāri.

Ta. tățți cleverness, skill, bravery, fluency. Ma. dhāți bold- Ka. dăți, dhăți quickness in writing, fluency in reading, practice in a science, haste. Te. dhāți fluency, rapidity, vigor. Skt. dhārstyaboldness, violence. Pkt. *dhāțha-, *dhāțhia-, or the like (cf. dhattha-, dhițțha- bold).

Ta. tāmpāļam salver of a large size. Ka. tāmbāla, tāmbāņa a metal dish. Tu. tämbana a metallic dish or tray. Te. tāmbālamu tray, salver. Mar. tāmhan a circular metal dish; tãblē, tabli a small metal drinking vessel. (Both are said by Kulkarni to be < Skt. tāmracopper).

Ta. tarai blade of weapon, sharpness. Ma. dhāra edge of a sword or instrument. Ko. ta'r sharp edge (of weapon, tool, stone). Ka. dhāre sharp edge of a sword or any cutting instrument. Tu. dhāre sharpness. Te. dhāra sharpness or edge of any cutting instrument. Go. (A) dhar edge of knife. /Skt. dhārā- sharp edge, blade.

Ta, tāvaļam lodging, place of residence; tāvu resting-place, lodging, shelter. Ma. tāvaļam lodging place, retirement, . Ka. tāvu, ļāvu, thāvu place, abode. Te. tävalamu id., home; tāvu place, locality, abode, residence; thāvu place, house, residence. /Skt. sthāman- place. Pkt. thāma-, Apabhramsa țhāma- id. H. thăw id. Mar. thāv id. Turner, s. v. thāū.
Ta. tālam cymbal. Ma. tālam id. Ka. tāla, tāla, tāņa id. Kod. tāļa id. Tu. tāla, tāla Te. tālamu id. id. Skt. tāla- cymbal. BHS tāda- id. Pa. tāla- id.

Ta. tikku direction; protection, shelter, aid. Ma. dikku direction, region; refuge. Ko. dik protection, aid. To. tik id. Ka. dikku direction; refuge, protection, help. Kod. dikkö direction. Tu. dikku direction; refuge, protection. Te. dikku id. Skt. diś- (nom. sg. dik) direction, country. id. DICTIONARY 41

Ta. aruttam, arttam meaning, intention, wealth, usefulness, etc. Ma. artham aim, wealth, meaning. Ko. artm (obl. art(t)-) meaning, a sententia, proverbial saying. To. artm (obl. art-) meaning, useful- Ka. artha aim, utility, meaning, wealth, etc. Tu. artha wealth, meaning. Te. arthamu meaning, object, wealth, use, etc. /Skt. arthaaim, use, object, wealth, meaning, etc. Ka. amaga 18 ness. 12 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN 22

Ta. titti bellows, purse, leather bag, a kind of flute or pipe; tuti bellows; tutti bass-pipe. Ma. titti bagpipe. Ko. tiod bellows. Ka. titti, tidi leather bag, bag in general, pair of bellows. Tu. sidi, sidè bellows; tuti a sort of drone corresponding to a bagpipe. Te. titti leather bag or case, a skin, any bag-like thing, bellows or pair of bellows, bagpipe. Kuwi (F) tittū (pl. 'nga) bellows; (S) tithunga id., bagpipes. Skt. dệti- leather bag, a skin, bellows. Pkt. *diti-, *didi-, dii- id.

Ta. tiru, ciri, ci śri, Lakşmi, holiness, sacredness. Ko. tir im the Toda ti:- buffaloes; tir er buffalo calf at Toda calf sacrifice; ciry prosperity, happiness of life. To, ti: the most sacred grade of Toda dairy; ti: ir the buffaloes of the ti'-dairy (i.e. the holy buffaloes). Skt. śri- Lakşmi, holiness, sacredness. Pkt. siri- id.

Ta. tuti (-pp-, -tt-) to praise, flatter, worship; n. praise, eulogy, fame. Ka. tuti, stuti praise, eulogy, flattery; tutisu, stutisu, stutiyisu to praise, worship. Kod. tudi- (tudiv-, tudiñj-) to be praised; (tudio-, tudic-) to praise. Tu. tuti, stuti praise. Te, stuti id.; stutincu to praise. /Skt. stuti praise, adulation. Skt. st- normally becomes Ta. t-, but there may be a MIA intermediary with th-, and also -d-, viz. *thudi-; Pa. thuti-, Pkt. thuti-, thui- are the attested forms.

Ta. turai chief, lord, master, ruler, gentleman, nobleman, European gentleman; turaicci, turaicāni lady, matron, mistress, European lady; turaittanam government. Ma. tura, dhvara master, lord, a man of rank. Ko. doyr European man; fem. dorca'ny. To. twary European (in songs). Ka. dore chief, king, master, a man of the ruling class; doresāni lady, mistress; doretana kingship, royalty, the rank or function of a king, government, rule. Kod. dore king, European. Tu. doré, dhore master, lord, king, ruler. Te. dora a chief, lord, ruler, governor, master, owner, an equal; doratanamu government, dominion, rule, reign, sovereignty. Pa. dora rich man, merchant, moneylender. Kuwi (S) doreesi gentleman. Skt. dhurya- leader, chief > dhaureya- superior > Pa. dhoreyya- (see Edgerton, BHS Dict., s.v. dhaura-), Pkt. dhoreya- (and dhojja-) id.

Ta. tulai steelyard, weight, well-sweep; tula id., balance, single shaft of a cart; tulām balance, steelyard, well-sweep, main beam in roof; tūlam beam of a house. Ma. tula balance; tulām id., beam, joist, sloping beam in a roof, well-sweep. Ko. tol log used in breaking bullocks to plow. Ka, tula, tule, tulā, tole balance, scales, weight, beams in roof of a house; dūla a beam of timber. Tu. tolè, tulè beam, log. Te. dūlamu beam. Kui tūli ridge of a house. /Skt. tula- bal- 42 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN ance, weight, a kind of beam in the roof of a house.
Ta. tūcu cloth, garment, cotton; tūcar washermen. Ka. dūsu, dūsa, dūşya cloth, cotton, calico. Skt. dūşya- a tent. . BHS důşyacloth, cotton. Pa. dussa- cloth, clothes. Pkt. dūsa- id.

Ta. tēti, teyti date, day of the month; titi lunar day. Ma. tiyyati, tiyati, tēti day of the month, date. Ko. te dy id. Ka, titi, tithi lunar day. Tu. tēdi a day of the solar month; tithi a lunar day. Te. tēdi a date, day of the month; tithi lunar day. Skt. tithi - lunar day.

Ta. tēvatāci, tēv-ațicci, tēv-ațiyāl temple dancing girl, prostitute. Ma. tēvațiyāļ id.; (vulg.) tēvițiyā- makan bastard. Ko. te vry prostitute; te vry mog son of a whore. /Skt. devadāsī- temple dancing girl (ațicci and ațiyāļ are calques on dāsī).

Ta. tēvu, tēvan god; tēvar deities; teyvam, taivam god. Ma. tēvan a deity. Ko. devr god. To, töw id. Ka. dēva id.; devva, devvu demon, evil spirit. Kod. de va god. Tu. dēva id.; daiva deity, god; devva demon, evil spirit. Te. dēva god; dēvara id., master; daivamu god. /Skt. deva- god; daiva-, daivya- divine. Pkt. devagod; devva divine.
Ta. arukkam crystal. To. ark glass (window or a piece of glass). Ka. arka crystal. Tu. arka id. Te. arkamu id. /Skt. arka- crystal.

Ta. tõņi boat, dhoney, ship, float, raft, canoe, water-trough. Ma. toņi trough, bathing tub, boat. Ka, dāņi, dāņi id. Tu, dāņi Tu. dõņi boat. Te. done a large boat, a small vessel or ship, (B also) a trough. Skt. droņi- wooden trough or tub, any vessel or implement made of wood. Pa. Pkt. doni- id., canoe. H. Joni small boat. Mar. doni Turner, s.v. duno, dunu. canoe. N id.

Ta. nakai jewels. Ma. naka jewel. To. naxy Ka. naga an ornament, an article, a piece, a load of articles, a bullock load. Kod. naga jewelry. Tu. naga jewels, ornaments; goods, property. Te, naga a jewel or ornament, a metal vessel, a bullock load of tobacco, etc. /Skt. naga- mountain. id., rock, precious stone, jewel. Mar. nag id., an article or item (as of implements, pieces of apparel, etc., in enumerating them), a piece. H. nag DICTIONARY 43

Ta. nankặram anchor. Ma. nankūram id. Ka. nangal, langar id. Tu. nangarų, nangalų, langarų id. Te. langaru id. Skt. nāgaraanchor (Tilakamañjarī, pp. 119, 122, etc.). Mar. nãgar id. H. langar id. ( Pers. langar). All ultimately < Greek öykūpa.

Ta. nattu nose-ornament. Ka. nattu id. Tu. nattų, nattu, nartu id. Te. nattu ring worn by women on the side of the nose. Go. (Muria) nath nosering. Skt. nastā hole bored through the septum of the nose; nastaka- septum of the nose (of cattle) or hole bored in it. Pkt. ḥatthānose-rope. H. nath nose-rope, a ring worn in the nose by women.

Ta. nāți pulse, artery, vein, tendon, ligament; nāri tubularity, tube, a measure of capacity (= 8 ollocks), Indian hour (= 24 minutes), weaver's shuttle, quiver, the 25th nakșatra; nārikai Indian hour. Ma. nāți, nāļi any tubular organ, vein, artery, the pulse; nāri tube, bamboo joint, a measure (of fluids); närikai an Indian hour. Ko, na ty pulse in wrist, sexual potency; na fy heart-beat, pulse. To. no ty pulse in wrist. Ka. nāļi any tubular organ of the body, as artery, vein, nerve, etc., the pulse; nāri Indian hour; nāļi tube, water channel, weaver's shuttle; lāļi weaver's shuttle. Tu. nāļi the pulse, a blood-vessel, artery, or vein; lali a weaver's shuttle. Te. nāļi any tubular organ of the body, artery, vein, the pulse. Skt. nāļi- any tubular organ (as a vein or artery of the body), pipe, tube, the pulse. Turner, s. vv. näril, nalil.

Ta. nāņayam stamped coin; uprightness, honesty, probity, honor as in money-dealings, punctuality, extraordinary facts or supposed facts in nature as of the cobra shrinking from the nāka-tāļi root, supposed virtue or action of a plant as the presenting of a herb to the eyes as a cure of ophthalmia, restriction, rule, that which is of good quality as a commodity; nāņakam stamped coin. Ma. nāņiyam, nāṇyam honesty, credit, what is current as reports, proverbs, coin, esp. gold coin. Ka. nāṇya fineness, goodness, good quality as that of grain, cloth, character, etc., honesty, truth, a coin, money, small pieces of silver money. Tu. nāṇya money, coin. Te. nāņemu a coin; honesty, trustworthiness; nãạemu quality, fineness, ascertaining the quality or fineness of anything, character, honesty; a coin; adj. fine, good, honest. /Skt. nāņakacoin or anything stamped with an impression. Pkt. ņāņaka-, ņāņaga- id.

Ta. nāyar a caste of Hindus in Malabar. Ma. nāyan, nāyar the Sūdras of Kēraļa; soldiers of all castes. Koờna'yammë a Nāyar man; fem. na'yarci. Tu. nāyare, näyimāre a Nāyar of Malabar. Skt. nāyaleader, chief.

Ta. nicam own; certainty, assurance, ascertainment, truth, veracity; nicavān true, sincere, upright, honest man. Ma. nijam own; cer- 44 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN tainty. Ka. nija innate, own; real, true, actual, genuine, real state or shape, reality, truth. Tu. nija own; truth, veracity, certainty, reality; true, certain, sure, real. Te. nijamu own; truth, reality, fact, truthfulness, veracity, certainty; true, real, actual, certain, positive; nija-padu to be verified, proved real or true; nija-paracu to realize; prove, establish; nijamari a truthful man; nijamugă truly, really, actually; nijāyati (coll.) truthfulness, honesty, uprightness. Kuwi (S) nizomi (z j) truth. /Skt. nija- innate, own.

Ta. nimpam margosa. Ma. nimpam Melia azadirachta. Ka. nimba Azadirachta indica Juss. Te. nimbamu id., neem or margosa tree. Pa. līm id. Go. (Muria) nimbu, (A) lim id. Kui lima the nim tree. Skt. nimba- Azadirachta indica. [M. azadirachta Linn. - A. indica Adr.)

Ka. nimbi, nimbe, limbe the acid lime, Citrus medica. Tu. nimbe, limbi, limbe the lemon fruit, C. bergamia. Te. nimma the lime tree. Kol. nimba lime, lemon; (SR) limbū lemon. Ga. (S) nimbe lime tree. Kui lembu lemon, lime. Kuwi (F) limba lemon; (S) limma lime, lemon. Skt. nimbū(ka)- the common lime, C. acida. Turner, s. v. nibu. Mayrhofer, s. v. nimbū-. C. medica Linn.; var. 1 medica proper (the citron); var. 2 limonum (the lemon); var. 3 acida (the sour lime of India); var. 4 limetta (the sweet lime of India). C. aurantium Linn.; var. 1 aurantium proper (the sweet orange); var. 2 bigaradia (the bitter or Seville orange); var. 3 bergamia (the bergamotte orange). ]
Ta. allam, nallam ginger; ? ellam id. Ka. alla green ginger. Te. allamu id. Kuwi (S) alomi ginger. Skt. ārdra(ka)- fresh ginger. Pkt. alla-, allaa- id. Mar. ălē id. Turner, s.v. aduwa.

Ka, nepa, neva, nevana, nevanu pretence, pretext, plea. Kod. neva"na pretence. Tu. nevana pretence, pretext, trick. Te. nepamu, nevamu id.; blame, imputation, charge, accusation. Skt. nibhasembling; (at end of bahuvrīhi cpds.) appearance, pretext. BHS, Pa. nibhāappearance, sheen. Pkt. ņihă- deceit; ņivva- pretence (DNM). Nepali ni(h)ũ excuse, pretence (see Turner).

Ta. nēmi (-pp-, -tt-), niyami (-pp-, -tt-) to appoint; nēmam appointment. Ma. niyamikka to order, appoint; nēmam rule, service of a raja. Ko. ne'mc- (ne.mc-) to select, appoint. Ka. nēma, niyama appointment; nēmisu, niyamisu to appoint. Tu. nēmaka appointment; determination, choice; nēmisuni to appoint, determine. Te. nēmincu, niyamincu to determine, fix, appoint, commission; nēmamu, (K also) nimamu rule, religious regulation. Go. nēmānā to obey instructions regarding diet in illness; (Ph.) nemanā to observe vows. /Skt. niyamarule, regulation; agreement, arrangement; etc. H. niyam, nem reid. DICTIONARY 45 P, B ace. . near.

Ta. pakațai ace upon dice. Ma. pakața, pakița id. Ka. pagade a mark on a die, a die or piece for playing backgammon, the play itself. Kod. pagade chess. Tu. pagade Te. pagada id. Mar. pagdā a draught (in the game). Connected with Mar. pag square on a chessboard, etc., which is undoubtedly the same as pag foot; on the very uncertain origin of this, Turner, s. v. pagdandi.

Ta. pakkam side, nearness; pakkal side, one's class or tribe. Ma. pakkam, pakkal, pakku side. Ko. pak, in phrases: tan paka'ſ by himself, of his own accord, tam paka'ſ with one another, etc. To. pak side. Ka. pakka, pakke, pakku id., proximity. Kod. pakka Tu. pakke side. Te. pakka side; near, adjacent; pakkiya side; ? prakka side, part, direction. Ga. (oll.) paki side. Skt. paksa- wing, side, proximity. Pkt. pakkha- id. Turner, s. v. pākho. b Ta. pakși, pațci, pakki bird. Ma. pakși, pakki id. Ko. paky id. Ka. pakși, pakki, hakki id. Kod. pakši, pakki id.; penis of immature boy. Tu. pakki bird. Te. pakși, pakki id. Ko. paksiak male bird; paksin female bird ( Mar.; tatsama from Skt.). Skt. pakşinbird. Pa, pakkhin- id. Pkt. pakkhi- id.

Ta. pankāru, pankāram, vankāram gold. Ko. banga'ry jewels, gold or silver chain. Ka. bangāra, vangāra gold; ongāra id., gold ornaments. Tu. bangārų, bangāra gold. Te. bangāru, bangăramu, bangaruvu id. Kol. (SR) bangār id. Konda baŋaram id. Kuwi (F) bangara, (S) bangăra id. /Skt. bhạngāra- gold pitcher or vase; gold (lex.).
Ta. pankuni month Phalguni (February March). Ma. pankuni id. Skt. phālguna- the month of the phalguni asterism. Pa. Pkt. phagguņa-

Ta. paccavațam, paccatam a long piece of cloth used as a blanket, bedsheet, or screen. Ma. paccavațam an entire piece of cloth (32 cubits); blanket. Ko. paca'd (obl. paca't-), paca'd vara'ſ cloak sewed together from two lengths. Ka. paccavaļa, paccada a stout cotton cloth (24 cubits long and 2 cubits broad), used as a wrapper or cover at night. Kod. paccada white cloth for saris. Tu. paccade shawl. Te. paccadamu bed sheet, cloak. /Skt. pracchada a cover, wrapper, blanket. Pkt. pacchaa- garment, sheet. Cf. entry 241 for vațam, etc. < Skt. pața-.
Ka. pañju torch. Tu. pañji, pañju id. Te. panju, panjāyā id. H. panji a sort of torch with five branches for lights (< Pers.).

To. poz ( cloak (only in stories). Ka. pañce, pañjā, pañje a small dötra used for various purposes. Kod. pañce waist-cloth. Te. 46 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN pance a man's lower garment. /Mar. pañcā a short dhoti ( Pers.).
Ta. pațanku standard, large banner. Ma. patannu flag. Te. . padaga id., banner. Skt. patākā-, pațākā- flag, banner. BHS pațākāid. Pa. patākā-, pațāka- id. Pkt. padāga-, padãā- id.

Ma. avakațam, apakațam mischief, danger. Ka. avagada, avagadike obstruction, jeopardy, monstrosity. Tu. avagada calamity, mischief, danger; disorder, confusion. Te. avakațamu Te. avakatamu opposition; avagadamu mischief, mischievous deed, carelessness, danger; bad, undesirable. Skt. avakața- opposite, contrary (so apparently in the lexica; taught in Pāṇini 5.2.30, but without meaning); L. V.R. 1934. 257. Mar. avaghad difficult, difficulty, calamity; avaghadņē to be in straits. Godavarma, p. 14: Skt. apakşta- injury, offence > Pkt. *apakața-. Cf. also 28 Ta. akațiyam.

Ta. pațam cloth for wear, painted or printed cloth, picture, upper garment; pațām cloth. Ma. pațam fine cloth, sheet, chequered cloth, picture. To. padm (obl. padt-) picture, photograph. Ka. pața, pada, padu cloth, chequered cloth, picture. Kod. pața picture. Tu. padambu a rough canvas cloth. Te. pațamu cloth, garment, picture. b Ta. pațțu silk cloth, silk yarn, sackcloth of Indian hemp; pațți cloth, puttee, bandage. Ma. pațțu silk, sackcloth made of hemp. Ko. patrag. To. poțy clothes. Ka. pațțu, pațța cloth, woven silk; patte, pațți silk . Kod. patti silk cloth. Tu. pațțè silk, piece of cloth, tape; pațți strip of cloth. Te. pațța, pațțā sackcloth; pațțamu silk thread; pațțu silk; patte tape. Skt. pața- cloth, garment, painted cloth, picture; pați- a kind of cloth; pațța- cloth, colored or fine cloth, woven silk. Turner, s.v. pāta.

Ta. pațāy vain pomp, bragging. Ko. bara'y haughtiness; bara'yga'rn haughty man. Ka. baļāyi vain pomp, bragging. Kod. bada'yi pride, self-conceit. Tu. baļāyi, pațāvu, pattanna, pațțanga boasting, bragging. Te. badāyi id., egotism, pride. H. barhāi increase, aggrandizement. Turner, s. vv. barāĩ(Nepali and some other languages have meaning 'boast') and baſāunu.

Ta. pați (-pp-, -tt-) to learn, study, read, recite, chant, say, tell, praise; pațippi (-pp-, -tt-) to teach; pațippu learning, study, reading, chanting, instruction. Ma. pațikka to learn, read, teach; pațittam, pațippu learning; pațippikka to teach. education. Ka. pațhisu, pathiyisu to read or repeat aloud, recite, study, express. Kod. paļi- (padip-, padic-) to learn. Tu. padipuni id. Te. pațhincu to read, recite. Kur. paſhnā to read, recite formulas. Malt. parye to read. /Skt. path- to read, study, learn, recite. Pkt. padh- id. H. paſhnā id. Turner, s. v. parnu.
Ta. pațikkam, pațiyakam spittoon, pot for receiving water used for an idol. Ma. pațikkam spittoon. Ka. padiga id. Tu. padlậlya id. Te. paạiga id. /Skt. pratigraha- spittoon. Pkt. padiggaha- id.

Ta. pațikkāram, pațuki alum. Ma. pațikkāram, pațikakkāram id. Ka. pațigăra, pataka, patika, patike id. Tu. pațikära id. Te. paţikāramu, patika, pațiki id. /Skt. sphaţikā-, sphaţikārð- alum. Turner, s.v. phaſkiri.

Ta. pațu clever skillful person, sound intellect. Ma. patu clever, Ko. paryp DICTIONARY 47 a smart. Ko. bat feat, clever deed; batga:rn clever man, winner. To. potxo'rn clever person. Ka. pašu clever, skillful. Tu. pațy id. Te. pațuvu id. /Skt. pațu- clever, skillful, cunning.

Ta. pațțam plate of gold worn on forehead as an ornament or badge of distinction, title of office or dignity, regency, reign. Ma. pattam ornament of the forehead, diadem, high dignity, ordination and tonsure. Ko. pațm (obl. pațt-) diadem, title. To. pot crown; poțm (obl. poţt-) throne, title, power, ability. Ka. pațța frontlet with a golden tablet with which king is decorated at coronation, royalty, royal throne, dignity, office. Kod. patta inauguration as king. Tu. pațţa crowning, ordination, throne, rank. Te. pațţamu coronation, frontlet, tiara, diadem, a title; pațți frontlet. Skt. pațța- frontlet, tiara, diadem.

Ta. pattayam, pațțaiyam, pațțā, pațțā-kkatti sword; pațțam id., weapon; pațțicam weapon. . Ma. pațțayam broad sword; pațțasam, pațțiśam sharp-edged spear, Ka. pattaya, pațe, pattā a long and broad sword; pațțiśa, pațțisa spear with a sharp edge. Te. pațţă-katti double-edged sword; pattiyamu, pațțemu sword; pațțisamu a sort of weapon. /Skt. pațțiśa- spear with a sharp edge or some other weapon with three points. H. pață a long, broad sword with two edges; a wooden foil; patti a foil. Cf. Skt. pattra(ka)- blade of sword or knife, knife, dagger.

Ta. pațțan brahman priest of a temple. Ma. pațțan a class of foreign brahmans, often traders. Ka. bhatta, batta, bața a learned brah- Kod. paštë brahman; fem. pațțati; adj. paſta. Tu. bhatte, batte priest, soothsayer. Te. bhațțūdu title affixed to the names of learned brahmans. Skt. bhatta- lord; part of the name of a learned brahman.

Ko. baty pile of wood covered with earth by which charcoal is made. Ka. bațți kiln, furnace, still. Tu. batti id. Te. batti a still. /Skt. bhrăştra- gridiron. Pkt. bhattha- id. H. bhatt(h)i distillery, furnace, kiln.

Ta. avacaram favorable opportunity; hurry, urgency, necessity, compulsion. Ko. avca.rm (obl. avca'rt-) hurry, urgency. To. ofso'rm id. Ka. avasara necessity, urgency, hurry; avasarisu to make haste, be eager. Tu. avasara, avasāra, amasara necessity, urgency, hurry. Te. avasaramu occasion; necessity, need, urgency, haste, hurry; necessary, urgent; avasara-padu to hurry, hasten. Skt. avasara favorable opportunity, seasonableness. L. V. R. 1934, 258.

Ta. paņam wealth, coin, money, sp. coin (fanam) of varying local values. Ma. panam coin, fanam, money; paņa-ttūkkam weight of a gold fanam. Ko. paņm (obl. pant-) money; four-anna piece. Ka. pana a small coin of silver or gold (fanam), wealth. Kod. paņa money. Tu, paņăvu 1/4 rupee, money, wealth; paņa-tūka the weight of a gold fanam. Te. paņamu a certain copper coin or its weight, wealth. Skt. pana a weight of copper used as a coin.
Ta. paņțāram religious mendicant, Saiva monk. Ma. pantāram Shaiva mendicant. Te. paņdāram n. of a certain caste. /Skt. piņdārareligious mendicant. man. 48 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN S.V.

Ko. baty cigar. To. paty id. Ka. batti id. Tu. batti id. /Skt. vart- anything rolled or wrapped round; dhūpa-varti-, dhumavarti a kind of cigarette. Cf. H. batti ( Skt. vart-), but not in this meaning.

Ta. panti row, series, line of persons seated for dining; stable for horses or elephants. Ma. panti row, esp. of feast-guests; range of buildings, stable; arrangement, order, Ko. pandy row of leaves with food at dry-funeral feast. Ka. panti, pante, panni row, series, row of people sitting down at a meal. Tu. pantè id. Te. banti a row, line, rank. Skt. pańkti- row, series, company (e.g. of persons eating together or belonging to the same caste). Pa. Pkt. panti- id. Turner, pãti.

Ta. paravā care, concern, harm. Ma. parava concern, care. Ko. parva:dy ila', parva'y ila: it doesn't matter, it is a little good, it's all right. Ka. paravā, parave, parvā care, concern about, regard, heed, anxiety; paravā illa it is of no consequence, never mind. Kod. paruva ille it doesn't matter. Tu. parava, parva concern, care, regard, respect. Te. parvā regard, respect, care for; parvā lēdu never mind, no matter. Br. parvā care, concern ( Pers.). / H. parwă care, concern, anxiety (< Pers.).

Ta. parāmari (-pp-, -tt-) to examine, consider; take care of, maintain, support, cherish, conduct (as an office), discharge (as duties); parāmarippu maintenance, support, management; parāmarici (-pp-, -tt-) to consider. Ma. parāmarsikka to consider; take care of. Ko. para'vary a cure, cured. Ka. parāmarśisu, parāmarisu, parāmbarisu, parāmmarisu to examine, be considerate; treat or attend kindly, tend or take care of, console. Tu. parāmbaripuni to consider; take care of, nurse; parāmbarikè investigation; care, protection. Te. parāmarsincu, parāmarisincu to examine, inquire after; condole with, console; parāmarśamu, parāmarika, parāmarisa examination, inquiry; attentions, care, condolence. /Skt. parāmṛść to lay hold of, touch, consider, deliberate. BHS parāmrs- (see Edgerton, BHS Dict. for meanings). Pa. parāmas- to touch, hold on to, deal with, be attached to or fall a victim to. Pkt. parāmaristo consider, touch (so Sheth).

Ta. parvam, paruvam knot, joint, the five religious ceremonial days in each fortnight, festival. Ma. parvvam, paruvam knot, joint, period, festival. Ko. pabm festival in February-March (Kota Texts, text 41); parv feast given in payment of vow, to avert ill consequences of transgression, or on being readmitted to caste. To. parf feast given by Badagas once a year to which Todas go. Ka. parva, parba festival, DICTIONARY 49 holiday. Tu. parba, pabba , id. . Te. pabbamu feast. Ga. (S) parrūb (pl. parbūl) festival. Kur. parab, parbī festival, feast. Malt. parbe festival. /Skt. parvan- knot, joint, the days of the changes of the moon, sacrifice (or festival] at a change of the moon, festival. Pkt. pavvaid. H. parb, parab id.

Ta. palakai plank, board; long shield. Ma. palaka plank, board; seat, footstool; shield. Ko. palg, pal plank; bench in main room of house. Ka. palage, palige, parige plank, board; shield. Kod. paleya wooden stool. Tu. palăyi plank, board. Te. palaka plank; bench. ? Pa. pakki stool. Br. palk plank. Skt. phalaka- board, wooden bench, shield. Pkt. phala(g)a-, phalaha- id. Turner, s.v. phaliyo.

Ta. paļinku crystal, crystal quartz, mirror. Ma. palunku crystal, glass. Ka. paļuku, palaku, paliku, palika crystal. Te. (B) palugu rock crystal. /Pa. phaļika- crystal. Pkt. phaliha- id. Pkt. phaliha- id. Sgh. paļiňgu id. (Skt. Sphatika-; Master, BSOAS 11.297 ff.).
Ta. pākār fort wall. Ka. pāgal, pāgala, păgăra encircling wall, rampart. Tu. pāgăra inclosure, fence, rampart. Skt. prākāra- wall, rampart. Pa. pakāra- id. Pkt. pāgāra-, pāāra- id.

Ta. avati limit; suffering, distress. Ma. avadhi-ppețuka to be pressed Ka. avadhi limit; extremity, calamity, misfortune. Te, avadhi (B.; coll.) calamity, misfortune; (K) avadhĩ-bettu to put to trouble; avadhĩ -bovu to be troubled, perish, go to waste. /Skt. avadhi- term, limit. L. V.R. 1934, 257-8.
Ta. pāku treacle, molasses, coarse sugar, palm sugar; any liquid food. Te. pāgu, pākamu, (K also) paku melted sugar, syrup, candy. /H. pāg syrup. Skt. pāka- is origin of Te, pākamu.
Ta. påkutam gift, present, royal revenue, tribute. Ka. pāvuda, pävada, pāguda a present. /Skt. prābhịta- gift. Pkt. pāhuộa- id.
Ta. pāccikai dice. Ma. pāccika id. Ka. pācike id. Te. pācika, pasika id. /Skt. pāśa(ka)- die. Turner, s.v. päso*. Mayrhofer, s.v. pāśakaḥ.

Ta. pāțakam anklet worn by women. Ma. pāțakam id. Ka. pädaga anklet worn by children and women. Tu. pādaga, pāduga anklet. Te. pādagamu silver anklet. Skt. pädakațaka- anklet. Pkt. *pāaadaga- > Dr. pādaga- (Godavarma, p. 205, gives a Pkt. pāagaďaga- (not found in the dictionaries] as the source; even though this might be expected, it is only *pāaadaga- that will contract to pädaga-).

Ta. påțai Indian pareira. Ma. pāța Cissampelus or Clypea. Ka. pädāvaļi-balli Clypea burmanni. /Skt. pāțhā- Clypea hernandifolia. Pkt. pādhā- id. (Prob. all the same species, but there has been considerable disagreement in the botanical terminology.)

Ta. pāțțiyami day after the full or new moon ( Te.). Ka. padya, pădiya, päţiva first day of a lunar fortnight. Tu. pädya id. Te. padyami id. /Skt. pratipad-, pratipada- first day of a lunar fortnight. Pkt. padivaā- id. H. pașiwā, pariwā id. Turner, s.v. parewa?. 50 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO- ARYAN

Ta. pāpam, pāvam sin, crime; an exclamation of pity. Ma. pāpam evil, sin; interj. alas! what a pity! Ko. pa pm (obl. pa'pt-) sin, injury; an exclamation of pity. Ka. pāpa sin, guilt; O misery! Kod. pa pa an exclamation of pity. Te. pāpamu sin, crime; alas! what a pity! / Skt. pāpa- sin, evil. L. V. R. 1935. 66.
Ma. pāļi tip of the ear. Ka. pāle, hāle, halle lobe of the ear. Tu. pāļi, pāļè tip of the ear. /Skt. pāli- lobe of the ear. Mar. pal outer curving edge of ear.
Ta. pāval wooden sandals. Ka. pāvuge, hāvuge, avuge, hävige, ävige shoe. Te. pāva (pl. pāvalu) a sandal. /Skt. pādukā- shoe. Pkt. pāuā- id.

Ta. pittu millet flour. To. it flour. Ka. pițțu, pițțe, hittu id., meal, powder. Tu. itļy flour. Te. pişța mu id., meal. Skt. pişța- crushed, ground; flour, meal. Pa. Pkt. pittha- id. Turner, s. v. pițho. b Ta. pittu, puțțu a kind of confectionery; piţtam dough. Ma. pittu, puttu a thin meal-cake, rice-bread. Ko. pițrice, ragi, etc, cooked so as to form a solid mass; food. To. it lump of boiled food other than rice; prț fried cake. Ka. pittu, pitte, hittu porridge (esp. of rāgi), food; puțțu salted dough baked. Kod. puțții a preparation of rice, wheat, or other grain. Tu. hitty porridge. Te. pittu flour boiled in steam. Skt. pișța- kneaded; cake, pastry; pișțaka- cake or anything made of flour (lex.). BHS pişțaka- cake. Turner, s. v. pițho.

Ta. avantarai disorder, confusion, forlornness, becoming useless, fruitless. Ka, abandara, abandare disorder, irregularity, uselessness, waste. Te. abandara disorder, confusion, irregularity. /Skt. abandhuram dejectedly, sadly (śiśupālavadha 6.29; comm., - aśobhana-).

Ta. pittaļai brass. Ma. pittaļa, piccaļa id. Ka. pittala, hittăți, hittăle id. Tu. pittalè id. Te. pittaļamu, pittalamu, ittadi, ittaļi id. Kol. pitol, (Hislop) pital id. Kui pitalo id. Kuwi (F) pītara, (s) pittada Kur. pitali, pitali id. Malt. piteli id. /Skt. pittala-, pitala- brass, bell-metal. Pkt. pittala- id. H. pītal id. Mar. pita! id. Turner, s. v. pital.

Ta. pirațai, piruțai plug of a lute, screw-nut. Ka. birade, birade peg or screw to tighten the strings of musical instruments; a cork. Te. biradă a cork, stopper, plug, peg. Mar. birdē a button and/or loop. Turner, s.v. biro, birko, for some items that may be connected.
Ta. pirukkam kidney. Ko. viky id. To. pïşk id. Br. bik kidney (Bray: borrowing from Jațki buk, Si. bukī). Skt. vřkka- kidney. Pa. Vakka id. NIA in general has forms with -u-; Turner, s.v. boknu.
Ta. puttam buttocks; pudendum muliebre; puțți waist. To. pïty buttocks. Skt. prstha- back. Pkt. puţtha- id. H. puţthā buttock. Turner, s.v. pith.

Ta. pūci (-pp-, -tt-) to perform acts of ceremonial worship; id. DICTIONARY 51 worpūcai worship. . Ma. pūjikka to honor, worship; pūja worship. To. pu'z- (pu'j-) to do worship at temple. Ka. pūjisu to worship; pūje worship. Kod. pu'j- (pu'ji-) to do the acts of worship. Tu. pūjè ship. Te. pūjincu to worship. Skt. pūj- to honor, worship; pūjāworship.

Ta. pūri (-pp-, -tt-) to be full, become perfect, thrive, abound; fill (tr.); puri (-pp-, -tt-) to fill up (tr.), inlay; purai (-pp-, -tt-) to be great; n. greatness, height, eminence. Ma. pūrikka to fill, accomplish; be full. To. pūry- (pürs-) to become full; pürc- (pürč-) to fill (tr.). Ka. pūray(i)su, pūravisu, pūrisu to fill, fill up, complete, fulfil; be filled, be completed, finished, be accomplished; pura, puru much, many, abundant. Tu. puresuni, pũraisuni to complete, fulfil, be satisfied, afford. Te. pūragincu to fulfil, accomplish; pūrincu to fill (tr.). Pa. pūr- to be completed. Kui pūri full; pūri āva to be full; pūri giva to fill; prusu full, filled; prusu inba to be full, filled; prusna fully. Kur. purnā Kur. pārnā to have reached one's full measure, perfection or numbers, be finished, be sufficient, enough, bear all the expenses for the maintenance of; purtī fully what is required, sufficiency; pūrem perfectly, entirely. Malt. púrare to be fulfilled; púratre to complete, fulfil. Br. pūra full, complete, fulfilled. Skt. půray- to fill, complete, fulfil. Turner, s. v. purnu, puro; NIA has both long-vowel and shortvowel forms.

Ta. pēțțai extramural suburb, marketplace near a town; pēļu small town, village. Ma. pēțţa suburb. Ka. pēțe market town, a long street of shops in a town. Kod. pe:țe bazaar. Tu. pētè, pēntè id, Te. pēța suburb or division of a town, town. /Mar. peth, pēth trading town, market, long street of shops, large division of a city.

Ta. poțțaņam, poțțaņi, poţtalam, poțţali small bundle, parcel. Ka. pottana, potna, pottaļa, poţia a small cup or packet made of leaves, paper, etc. Te. poțlamu packet, bundle. Go. (Ph) poțri bundle. /Skt. poț(t)ala- bundle, packet. Turner, s.v. poți (where Sgh. poţtaniya is quoted). Mayrhofer, s.v. poțalah.

Ta. pokaņi, pokiņi a kind of drinking cup or water vessel. Ko. bo'giny, bo'giņdy metal drinking vessel. Ka. bögani, böguņi metal basin for washing or culinary purposes. Tu. böguņi small saucepan. Te. bögāņi, bògiņi a sort of copper or brass bowl or cup. /Mar. bahuguņē, bahuguni, bogaņē, bogani, bogoņē, bogoņi, etc. broad-mouthed metal vessel.

Ta. pokam enjoyment, eating, prosperity. To. po'x pair-word festival; ? po'xo'rn clever man. Ka. bhöga, boga enjoyment, feasting, wealth. with pa'n 52 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN feasting, wealth. /Skt. bhoga- enjoyment, eating, object of enjoyment (as festival), wealth.
Ta. aniram, anutam, anuşam the 17th nakṣatra (i.e. lupus and scorpion's head). Ma. anuram id. Skt. anurādhā- id. Ā
Ta. pol hollow object, bamboo. Te. bölu hollow. /Pkt. pollahollow. H. pol hollowness. Turner, s.v. pwāl. These and other IA words have been given Dravidian origin in DED 3726.

Ta. põnakam, ponam food, boiled rice, eating; põnakatti female cook, feeding nurse; põņam food. Ka. bona id., boiled rice; bõnagitti woman who cooks for strangers and travelers. Tu. bona food. Te. bonamu id., boiled rice, eating; bõnakõļu, būnamukāļu a cook; fem. bonakattiya, bõnakatte, bõnamukatte. /Skt. bhojana- eating, meal, food. Pkt. bhoaņa-, bhona- id. M
Ko. mand liquid honey in bee-hive. Ka. manda the spirituous part of wine, spirituous liquor. Skt. manda- the spirituous part of wine.

Ta. maņțakam cake of flour prepared without sugar; manţikai a cake. Ka. mandaka, mandage, mandige a cake or bread of wheaten flour. Tu. mandige a kind of very thin cake. Te. mandiga a sort of biscuit made of wheat. /Skt. mandaka a sort of pastry or baked flour. Pkt. mamda(g)a- id.

Ta. mati understanding, judgment, esteem, value; (-pp-, -tt-) to estimate, value, esteem, reverence, think, decide; matippu estimate, esteem, respect, intention. Ma. mati the mind, understanding, estimation, reasonable amount, enough; matikka to appraise, estimate, esteem; matippu valuation. Ko. madc- (madc-) (woman) obeys, respects (husband). Koș. madi Kod. madi enough. Tu. madipuni to consult, deliberate, settle; madipu consultation, settlement, resolution. Te. matincu, madincu to esteem, appraise; matimpu, madimpu estimating, valuation, Skt. matithought, the mind, understanding, esteem.

Ta. matu, maturam sweetness; maturi (-pp-, -tt-) to be sweet. Ma. madhuram sweet; sweetness; madhurikka, madhộkka, matskka to be sweet. Ka. madhu, madu, madhura sweet; sweetness. Kod. modï- (modip-, modit-) to be sweet; modira sweetness. Tu. madhu madhura, madura sweet. Skt. madhu-, madhura sweet.

Ta. mattari, mattalam, mattaļi a kind of drum. Ma. maddalam a long finger-drum, tambourine. Ka. mad(d)ale, maddale, madle, mardala, mardale a kind of drum, tabor, Tu, maddoli a finger drum. Te. maddela a kind of drum. Kui mordolo id. /Skt. mardala a kind of drum. Pkt. maddala- id. id.; DICTIONARY 53

Ta. mattu, mattam, mantam churning staff. Ma. mattu id., a rammer; mantu, mantham churn-staff, wooden beater. To. mod, (in songs) mode ry churnstick. Kan manta id.; mantu, mantha id., churning. Tu, mantų, manta churning stick. Te. manthamu id. /Skt. manthan- (allomorph mathin-), mantha- id.

Ta. mayilai foulness, dirt; ash color, grey, mixed color of white and black as of cattle. Ka. maylige impurity, dirt, dirtiness, a dirty thing; maylu impurity, dirt, dinginess, dark-huedness; mayle dirt, foulness, dirty. Tu. maile filth, pollution, dirtiness; dirty, filthy, foul. Te. maila dirt, foulness, filth, uncleanness, impurity, pollution, defilement. /Pkt. maïla- dirty. H. mailā id. Turner, s.v. mailo.

Ta. mariyātai, maricāti, maruvāti boundary, limit, courtesy, reverence, propriety of conduct, caste rules or customs. Ma. maryāda, mariyāda (d, not t) limit, boundary, custom, propriety, civility. Ko. marva'dy, mara'dy respect, self-respect. To. marj, marsoồy respect for another. Ka. maryāde, mariyāde limit, boundary, established rule or custom, propriety of conduct, respect. Kod. maria di custom (of a village, etc.); honor, respect. Tu. maryādi, mariyādi, mariyādè custom, usage, propriety of conduct, respect, a present. Te. maryāda, mariyada id., limits or bounds. /Skt. maryādā- frontier, limit, bounds of morality and propriety, custom.

Ta. manitan, manican, manucan, manittan man; maniccar men, human beings; maniccu manliness. Ma. maniccan servant, slave; manitan a person of rank. male human being; fem. mancc. To, monsn human being, man. Kod. manžšë Tu. man(u)se pariah. Te. (K) manişi a person. Skt. manuşya-

Ta. manni (-pp-, -tt-) to forgive, pardon; mannippu pardon, forgiveness. Ko. manc- (manc-) to pardon; manyp pardon. (monc-) to forgive. Ka. mannisu to honor, reverence, show kindness, treat with kindness and respect, pardon; mannane respect, politeness. Tu. mannipuni, mannisuni to forgive, pass over, overlook, regard, treat kindly, honor, show respect; mannanè respect, civility, politeness, attention. Te. mannincu to respect, honor, treat with respect, esteem highly, care for; excuse, pardon; mannana respect, politeness, courtesy; mannimpu respecting, showing respect to, excuse, pardon, forgiveness; mannike respect. /Skt. man- (present 3 sg. manyate) to honor, esteem. Pkt. mann- id. Turner, s.v. mānnu.
Ta. månkicam meat, flesh. To. mo'xcm (moxct-) id. /Skt. māmsa- id. (in its pronunciation māŋsa-).

Ta. maci the eleventh solar month, January-February. Ka. māgi, Ko. mancn man. a nan. To. mony- 54 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN a māge the cold season, coldness. Tu. māyi the eleventh Tuļu month January- February. /Skt. māgha- id.

Ta. mānavakan celibate student, pupil, scholar, religious student, lad more than eight and less than sixteen years of age, fool, inexperienced person; māņavan, māņākkan celibate student, scholar, pupil; māņākki female disciple, school girl; māņi student, bachelor; dwarf. Ma. māņavan, māņavakan boy, student; māņi manikin, boy, the child of a Nambudiri, a young Brahmin student. Ka. māņava, māni a youth, lad; māņavaka id., pupil. Tu. māņi a brahman boy; māni, māņi man, a messenger, servant. Te. māņavakūļu a boy or lad not exceeding sixteen years of age. /Skt. māņava(ka)- youth, lad (esp. a young brahman), manikin.

Ta. mätiri pattern, example, sample, specimen, model; manner, way; kind; mātirikai id.; the original as distinguished from a copy. Ko. ma'dyr, ma:dyrm (obl. ma:dyrt-) fashion, manner, way; kind. To. mo. Biry model, sample, fashion. Ka. madiri the original from which a copy is made, a pattern, specimen, sample. Tu. mādiri, mādri a specimen, sample, pattern. Te. mādiri, mādari, mādri id., model, type, example, original, prototype, sort, kind, species, variety. Skt. mātņkā- mother, source, origin, (acc. to Kitt.) the original from which the copy (putrike) is made. L. V.R. 1935.70.

Ta. mari death, smallpox, goddess of smallpox, Durgā. Ma. māri a plague, esp. smallpox; a bore, intolerable person. Ka. māri killing, plague, epidemic, the goddess of death, Durgā; mārikā plague, cholera. Tu. māri the goddess presiding over epidemic diseases, a plague, epidemic, smallpox; a bore, intolerable person. Te. māri plague, pestilence, epidemic; a form of the goddess Durgā supposed to preside over epidemic disease. / Skt. māri- death, pestilence, smallpox; mārikā- plague, pestilence.

Ta. mānam shame, disgrace; māni (-pp-, -tt-) to become ashamed, be bashful; mānipam shame. Ma. mānam bashfulness. Ko. ma'nm (ma'nt-) feeling of shame, disgrace; ma'nişțm disgrace. Te. mānamu self-respect, shame. /Skt. māna- pride, a wounded sense of honor.
Ta. miriyam, miriyăl pepper. Te. miriyamu, miremu, miriyālu (pl.) black pepper. Pa. miri pepper. Skt. marica- pepper. Pkt. maria-, miria- id. H. miri id. Turner, S. v. maric.

Ta. munțam head, forehead, clean-shaven head, bald head, skull; headless trunk, limbless body, undeveloped foetus, naked body, useless person, blockhead, globe, sphere, stump, stake; munțan shaven-headed a DICTIONARY 55 person, Śiva as having a skull in the hand; barber; muntanam shaving of the head; munți person with clean-shaven head; barber; munțitam shaving the head clean; munțai widow as having a shaven head. Ma. . mundam a pollard, a bald-pate, shaved; munda widow with shaved head; mundanam shaving the head; mundi barber; a bald head; munditam shorn, lopped (d, not t). Ko. mundņ widower; mundo, mundgeyſ, mundgeyệc, mindgeyſ, miņdgeyệc widow. Ka. munda shaved, bald, having no hair on the head; man with a shaved head; hornless, destitute of some limb; stripped of leaves or branches, a pollard; headless body; bald pate; pointless, blunt; low, mean; barber; mundaka the lopped trunk or stem of a tree; barber; head; mundige post; mundu headless body; munde close-shaved woman, widow, harlot. Kod. munde widow. Tu. munda, mundu forehead, trunk; munţe widow. Te. munda id., prostitute; mundanamu shaving; mundi, munditūdu a bald-pate, bald-headed person, one who has a shaven head; barber; muſạitamu closely shaven, bald; mundūdu man with a bald or shaven head. /Skt. munda- bald, having the head shaved, hornless, lopped, blunt, low, mean; n. man with shaven or bald head; barber; mundā- widow.

Ta. ākāttiyam pretence simulating agony or injury, outrageous behavior such as threatening to commit suicide. Ka. agātya id. Te. āgātyamu, āgāyityamu outrageous behavior, obstinacy, a desperate act, pretence of agony or injury, impropriety. Prob. Skt. āghātay-; cf. esp. BHS āghāta- malicious feeling, anger, hatred.

Ta. akattiyam, akattiyam-āy without fail, surely, certainly. Ka. agatya indispensableness, necessity, want; agatyav-āgi necessarily, urgently, positively, by all means. Tu. agatya need, necessity, want; urgent, important. Te. agatyamu necessity, need; urgent, necessary, needful, important; agatyamu-gā urgently, necessarily, positively, certainly. Skt. agati want of resource, necessity, distress (so Kitt.); difficult from the point of view of meaning, whereas Skt. avaśyam, which corresponds exactly in meaning, presents phonetic difficulties (but not perhaps altogether insuperable).

Ta. mutta-kkācu, muttai straight sedge, Cyperus rotundus; straight sedge tuber, C. pertenuis; mucalai, muyalai fragrant tuber of C. rotundus. Ma, muttanna, mottenna a fragrant grass with medicinal bulb, C. rotundus, triceps. Ka. muste, musta, mustaka, musti C. rotundus Lin. and its tuber. Tu. muste C. rotundus. Te. musta, mustakamu, muste id. /Skt. musta(ka)- id. Pkt. mutthă- id. Turner, s.v. mothe. (Synonymy very complex. C. rotundus Linn. was never identified as C. pertenuis, though C. scariosus Br. = C. pertenuis Roxb. = C. rotundus Thw., and C. tuberosus Rottb. = C. rotundus Benth. = C. rotundus (tenuiflora) Thw. = C. rotundus, var. procerula, C. B. Clarke C. rotundus, var. acuta, Boeck. = C. pertenuis Bojer.)
Ta. mūcai crucible, earthen mould for casting molten metal. Ma. müsa id. Ka. musi, mūsi, mūse, mūşeid. Tu. mūsè, mūşè id. Te. mūsa, mūşa id. /Skt. mūşa- crucible.
Ka. mika, miga, mige wild beast, antelope. Te. mekamu, megamu beast, brute, antelope. Kol. (Kin.) mekam, (SR) měkām sambar. /Skt. mſga- wild beast, antelope. Pa. Pkt. miga- id.

Ta. mērai boundary, limit. Ma. mēra id. Ka. mēre edge. Tu. mērè boundary, limit. Te. mēra id.; mēraku according to, Kol. meira, (SR) merām /Mar. mēr edge, verge, margin, border (of a field, hill, etc.).

Ta. mocam treachery, deceit, fraud; danger, risk, detriment, id., up to. near. 56 DRAVIDIAN BORROWINGS FROM INDO-ARYAN accident; mistake, error; mócakkāran deceiver; moci (-pp-, -tt-) to err, be misled. Ma. mosam trick, deceit; fault, mistake; loss; māśakkāran trickster; blunderer; poor, sickly. Ko. mo'cm (obl. moʻct-) deceit, trick. Ka. mõsa, mösu id., fraud, duping, hypocrisy; blunder, fault, mistake; detriment, danger, peril; loss; mosagara, mosugara ceiver, a deceitful or treacherous man, a trickster; fem. mõsagārti. Kod. mo'sa deceit. Tu. mosa id., fraud, trick, dissimulation, treachery; fault, mistake; danger, risk; māsagāre deceiver, hypocrite. Te. mosa theft, deceit; mosagāļu deceiver, cheat; mösamu deceit, cheating, fraud, trick, duping; danger, harm, peril, jeopardy. /Pa. Pkt. mosauntruth, deceit < musā falsely (< Skt. mộșā); not from Skt. moșa- robbery, plundering (except in this meaning for Te.); cf. BHS mosa-dharma-, with hyper-Sanskritization (Edgerton, BHS Dict., s. v.; also Pischel $78); (L. V. R. 1935.70, wrongly).

Ta. mótiram finger-ring. Ma. mótiram id.; a collet for high caste children. Ko. mo·da'rm (obl. mo·da·rt-) ring; mudu:rm seal (esp. on ring). To. müdu•rm (obl. müdu·rt-) official's ring. Ka. modira, mudre ring. Kod. moyra id. /Skt. mudrā- ring, seal-ring. R

Ta. iravai small particle, coarsely ground wheat-flour, shot, diamond. Ka. rave a grain, granule, particle, small shot, grits. Tu. ravè id. Te. rava, (K also) ravva small particle, diamond; ravalu small shot. /H. rawā a grain, granule, grit, particle (< Skt. lava id.).
Ta. irānuvam army. Ma. rāņuvam id. Ka. rāņuve id. Te. rānuva id., retinue. /Cf. Skt. raņa- battle, war.
Tu. rave syrup made of sugarcane juice. Kol. (Kin.) ūsne rāp juice of sugarcane. Mar, rab boiled sugarcane juice. Turner, s. v. rābaſi. L

Ta. ācāri title adopted by Madhva and śri Vaişņava Brāhmans; title of the five artisan castes; ācān teacher, elder, priest; ācāļ priest's wife, lady of position; āciriyan priest, teacher, author of any literary work, scholar. Ka. ācāri title assumed by brahmin cooks, idol-makers, smiths, carpenters, goldsmiths, artificers. Kod. ayri (? a'yri) man of carpenter caste, blacksmith. Tu. acari a smith or carpenter. Te. acāri (= Ka.). /Skt. ācārya a spiritual guide or teacher. L. V.R. 1934. 259.

Ma. lakuka to soar; lätuka to leap. Ka. lāgu a leap, jumpi lāgisu to jump; lāga summerset. Tu. lāg(i)yuni to leap, jump, skip; DICTIONARY 57 läga, lāgya a jump, summerset. Te. lãgu a leap, jump, summerset; (K also) lãcu to pounce upon, attack, lie in wait. /Skt. langhay- to jump over. Pkt. langhe- id. H. lãghna id. Turner, s.v. nãghnu.

Ta. ilāvanam, lāvanam list of soldiers, of recruits, enlistment. Ma. lāvanam, lāvaņi list of soldiers, account-roll. Ka. lāvana a list of soldiers or of public servants. Te. lāvanamu enlistment, enrollment. /H. lāw banner ( Ar.). V

Ta. vakkaņam honorific superscription of a letter, words of courtesy, title, learning, scholarship, civilization, culture, order, taunt, accusation; vakkaņi (-pp-, -tt-) to expound in detail; vakkaņai honorific superscription of letter, words of courtesy, flowery or rhetorical speech, scholarship, culture, skilful talk; vakkāņam elaboration of a tune; vakkāņi (-pp-, -tt-) to expound in detail, carry on disputations. Skt. vyākhyāna- explaining, interpretation, narration. Pkt. vakkhāna- id. L. V.R. 1935.71.

Ta. vanku spreading spots on the skin, blotches on a mangy dog, hyena as spotted. Ka. bangu a disease of the skin in which it gets red, black and white spots. /Mar, vãg purple or dark discoloration of the skin, mole.

Ka. bañjaru waste land; bañje barren woman, barren cow, unproductiveness, barrenness. Tu. banjara sterile, barren; bañjè barren woman; barren, sterile. Ta. vațțam circle, circular form, wheel, cycle, circuit, curve, bend, a kind of boomerang; vaţtan round person; vațți (-pp-, -tt-) to be round in shape, revolve, gyrate, whirl, swing round, roll, throw as dice, bend; vațţikai circumference; vattu roundness, anything round, circular piece (used in game); vațțai felloe, rim of wheel. Ma. vaţtam circle, globe, roundness, cymbal, disk of sugar, potter's wheel, mill; broad space; adv. round; assemblage of things, preparation; aspect of things and circumstances; time, turn; vațțaņikka to go round; vaſtu a ball, round lump of metal, of sugar; rim of a wheel. Ka, bațța, baļļu that is round, circular, spherical or globular, a circle, disk, round mark on the forehead; bațțage roundness, round; bațţane in a turning-round manner, whirlingly; bațțanna round, circular; bațțitu, bațțittu that which is round. Kod. bațța round. Tu. batta a globe, sphere; adj. circular, round. Te. vatta the bar that turns the central post of a sugar mill; a testicle; vatra, vatrani round, circular; vațrana roundness; vațrincu to make round, cut into a round form or shape; vațruva, vațruvu circular, round, cylindrical, spherical, globular. b Ta. vațțakai small bowl, metal cup; vațţā plate, porringer, bowl; vațțil porringer, platter, plate, clepsydron. Ma. vațța cup, bowl, esp. a perforated cup for time-piece; vațțaka basin, platter, censor of metal; vațțalam large cooking vessel, brass pan. Ko. vat1 a metal eating-plate. Ka. battal, battala, baļķalu, bațla, batlu a concave, metal vessel, bowl, cup, basin, goblet. Kod. bațţa plate, small cup. Tu. battaly plate, esp. of bell-metal. Te. bațle a sort of earthen dish or plate. /Skt. vịtta(ka)- round. Pkt. vațța id. Turner, s.v. bāțā, bațlo(h)i.

Ta. vațți, vatļai, vețţi path, way. Ma. vațța id. Ka. batte, banțe id. Kod. batte id. Tu. battè id. ? Te, vența id.; manner, mode, business, subject. Skt. vartman- path, road. Pkt. vattă - id. H. batti id. Turner, s.v. bāțo.

Ta. vațțu small piece of cloth; vațțuțai cloth tied round the waist and reaching to the knee, garment. Ko, bat clothes. To. poty id. (in song; < Bad.). Ka. bațțe cloth. Kod. batte id., clothes. Tu. baţtè id. Te. bațța id. Skt. pațța- cloth (not Skt. vastra, which > Pkt. vattha-). Cf. entry 240b Ta. pațțu. DICTIONARY 59 To. pon

Ta. pațai (-pp-, -tt-) to serve (as food to guests), offer (as boiled rice) to gods or manes; vațți (-pp-, -tt-) to serve (as an item of a meal). Ma. pațekka to serve up, offer boiled rice to idols. Ka. badisu to help to food at meals, serve up or out; baạiga one who serves up as a meal. Te. vaddincu to serve or serve up as food; vaddana, vaddena serving food, placing food before one. /Pa. vadąheti gets ready (food), serves ( Skt. vệdh-); Mar. vāļhņē to serve (the food of a meal).
Ta. āți the fourth Tamil month, July-August; the 21st nakṣatra. Ma. āți id. Tu. āți id. Skt. äşāṇhā- the 21st and 22nd nakșatras.

Ta. vaņņam color. Ma. vaņņam id. Ko. vaņm (vaņt-) sari; large red cloth put over dead person. color; colored cloth with dots. Ka. banna color; dress, decoration. Tu. banna color. Te. vanniya, vanne id.; vanne cira a variegated cloth. Skt. varņa- /color. Pkt. vanna- id. Turner, s. v. bani?.
Ma. varuti news, report. Ka. varadi tidings, report, intelligence, communication. Tu. varadi, vardi, ordi news, report, intelligence. /Skt. vārttā- id. (so Kitt.).

Ta. vallayam a kind of spear. Ma. vallayam javelin. Ka. balya, balle, balleya, ballevu, balleha, bhalleya, bhāle a spear, pike, lance, javelin. Te. balle-kõla, ballemu spear. Pa. bala id. Kur, balam hunting-spear. Skt. bhalla a kind of arrow or missile. Pkt. bhalla-, bhallaa- id., spear. H. bhālā spear. Turner, S. V. bhālo.

Ta. vācam rafter. Ka. base id. Te. Vāsamu id. Kol. (Kin.) vāca beam. Pa. vācom horizontal beam across roof. Go. (M) vāsām rafter. , /Mar. vāsā, vãsā rafter, pole ( Skt. vamsa-). Turner, S. V. bãs. b Ka. vāsa flute, fife. Te. väse flute, pipe. Kol. vas flute. Nk. vacc (c = ts) id. ? Ta. vāy id. Skt. vamsa- bamboo, flute; vamśi- flute. H. bãsi id.

Ta. vāci difference, quality, nature, characteristic, fitness, propriety, good, improved condition, ground, cause, rate as of interest, portion, discount in changing money. Ta. vāțakai rent, hire. Ma. vāțaka id. To. po'doy rent (in song). Ka. bādage, bādige hire, rent, fare. Kod. ba'dige hire. Tu. bādāyi rent, hire, freight. Te. bāļiga hire, rent. / Skt. bhāța(ka). wages, hire, rent. Pkt. bhādaa- id. H. bhārā id., freight Turner, bhārā?.

Ta. vāțțam garden, street, way, road; vāțikai, vățakai district, street, garden, stable; vāți garden, courtyard, wall, village; vățai of houses, street, village; pāțțai road, way, conduct. Kui vāra a row of houses. /Skt. vāța- enclosure, fence, wall, garden, district, road; vățaka-, vāți-, văţikā- enclosure, garden. Pkt. vāda-, vādaga-, vāļi- id. Turner, s.v. bär?, bări?.
Ta. vāņam arrow; rocket, fireworks, fire. Ma. vānam arrow; rocket. Ka. bāņa id. Kod. baina Tu. bāņa id.; rocket. Te. bāņamu id. Skt. bāņa-, vāņa- arrow. H. ban id., rocket.
Ta, vāttu duck, goose. Ma. båttu id. Ko, va't goose. Ka. bātu, båte duck. Kod. ba ti id. Tu. battu id., gander. /H. bat, batak, batak duck (< Pers.).
Ta. Vāram days of the week, a week. Ma. vāram a week-day. Ko, va'rm (va.rt-) a week. Ka. vāra day of the week. Tu vāra a week. Te. vāramu id. /Skt. vāra- day of the week.

Ta. āņai command; oath (as in a court of justice), profane swearing, vow; āņaiy-iţu to issue an order, take an oath, swear. Ma. āņa command, oath, adjuration; āņay-ițuka to swear, adjure. Ka. āne mand; oath, adjuration; āņe idu to swear. Kod. a ne a curse; a'ạe idto curse. Tu. āne oath; āja oath, curse, swearing; āja korpuni to swear; āja pāņuni to curse. Te. ana order, command; oath, adjuration; ană-bettu to adjure. /Skt. ājñā- order, command; (L. V. R. 1934. 260). Pkt. āņaid. H. an id. Mar. āņ oath, vow. Turner, s. v. jännu (Add.).
Ka. bidiya shame, bashfulness. Tu. biļè id. Te. bidiyamu, bidemu id. Skt. vrid- to feel shame, be bashful. Pkt. vĩờia- ashamed.

Ma. vinta a copper pot for treasure. Ka. bindige a kind of metal water-vessel. Kod. bindige water-pot (for carrying). Tu. binde a small earthen pot. Te. bindiya, binde a metal pot. /Mar. bingā small metal vessel.

Ta. villai that which is circular, scented tablet, patch, a kind of ear-ornament (villai-muruku), metal badge on a peon's belt, a kind of id., DICTIONARY 61 any tablet head ornament, ball of cooked rice available in temples (villai-ccättam); pillai that which is round as a patch of sandal paste, a tablet or tabloid, nut of a screw, badge of a peon, square tile, a head ornament. Ma. villa a metal plate, a badge of peons. Ka. bille a circular object, a round plate of metal, etc., the breastplate of a belt as of a peon. Kod. bille gold plate worn by woman at back of head. Tu. billè anything made in a flat form as a tablet or lozenge, a peon's badge, etc., a pane, panel. Te. billa, billa a dish, a cake as of soap, etc., a small tablet or tabloid, a brass or silver plate used as a peon's badge, a round cushion or pillow, a bit or piece of silver or gold tied to the waist-thread of a female infant. Kuwi (F) bīla wheel; (S) billa button, wheel. H. billā or flat piece of metal, badge worn by peons.

Ta. veņķai, vaņțai okra, Hibiscus esculentus; esculent okra, Abelmoschus esculentus. Ma. vența H. esculentus. Ka. bende esculent okra or edible hibiscus, H. esculentus Lin. Tu. bendè esculent okra, A. esculentus; kādu bendè H. abelmoschus. Te. benda A. esculentus. Pa. bendi H. esculentus. Kui bendi (should be bendi) id. Kuwi bendi id. /Mar. bhēļā, bhēdi H. esculentus. Turner, s.v. bhīſā or bhērā. (H. esculentus L. - A. esculentus W. & A. H. Abelmoschus L. is different.)

Ta. ātēcam rule, command, precept. Ma. ādēsam order, command. Ko. a'de:cm (obl. a.de.ct-) allotted or fated span of life. To. o Dişțm (obl. o Biștt-) fore-ordained length of life, long life. Ta. āpācam fallacy, reflection; that which is filthy; apātan impure person, wicked man. Ma. ābhāsam low, vulgar. Ko. a'rabm work of cultivation. Ka. aramba, ārambu tillage, cultivation. Te. ārabamu vegetation, crops, (B also) cultivation, tillage. Prob. Skt. arambha- undertaking, beginning.

Ka. ārõgisu to eat; ārögana, ārögane eating, a meal. Tu. ārögane meal, repast. Te, āragincu to eat, drink; āraginta, āragimpu, ārögiņamu eating. /Pkt. aroggia- 'bhukta-' (DNM). Mar. arogan making a meal, eating.

Ta. ārccanam earning, acquisition; ārcci (-pp-, -tt-) to earn, acquire. Ma. arjanam acquiring. Ka. arjana, ārjane procuring, gaining; ărjisu to acquire, earn. Tu. ārjita acquired, inherited. Kur. arja'ānā to earn, gain (as a profit or advantage), acquire. Skt. arjto acquire, gain, earn. BHS ārjanā- winning, acquisition; ārjay- to win. . H. arjnā to acquire, earn; v.n. arjan. Turner, s. v. arjan and arjan.
Ta. avaại the 5th Tamil month, August-September; the 22nd nakṣatra. Ma. avaņi id. Ka. āvaņi id. Skt. śrāvaņa- id. Cf. 62 Ta. õņam.

Ta. akkiramam irregularity, injustice. Ma. akramam disorder, irregularity, crime. Ko. akrm (obl. akrt-) evil actions (? rather < Skt. akarman improper action, crime; cf. Ka. akarma id.). To. okira'm treachery. Ka. akrama confusion, injustice. Tu. akrama irregularity, confusion. Te, akramamu irregularity, misconduct, injustice, impropriety. /Skt. akrama want of order, confusion; (Bilhana, Vikramankadevacarita 14.11, 22) improper course of conduct.

Ta. asti property, wealth. Ma. asti id.; ästikäran wealthy. Ka. ăsti property, wealth; ăstika, āstigāra man of property. Kod. a'sti property. Tu. āsti property, wealth. Te. asti id.; astikādu wealthy man. /Skt. astimat- possessed of property, opulent. BHS asti (? ăsti), abstracted from sarvāsti 'all property.' 40 I

Ta. ițți, īțți spear, lance. Ma. itti stick, spear; iſti staff of spear, pike. Ko. ic sword, spear, sharp point. To. ițy, i'ty spear. Ka. içți, iți lance, spear, javelin. Kod. îțți ferrule of stick; i:ți, (Mercara) ï'ți spear. Tu. īți id. Te. ite, ſtiya id. Konda īța id. Kuwi (S) ite id. Skt. ſștí- spear, lance. Pa. ițțhi- id. Ta. ițţikai brick. Ma. ițţika id. Ko. it gal id. To. ițy, ity xal id. (in poetry). Ka. ițțige, ițțage, ițțangi, īțangi id. Tu. ittige id. Te. it(t)ika id. Kuwi (S) itteke illu tiled house. /Skt. iştakā-, işţikābrick. Pa. ițțhakā- id. Pkt. itthagā- id. U 43 ance.

Ta. ukkirāņam storehouse for provisions, granary; ukkirāņi storekeeper, steward. Ma. ugrānam (g, not k) storehouse, granary. Ka. ugrāņa id., treasury; ugrāņi storekeeper. Ta. uti (-pp-, -tt-) to swell, increase in size; rise, appear (as a heavenly body), come into existence, be born; utippu birth, appear- Ma. udikka (d, not t) to rise; udyal (d, not t) the rising sun. Ko. ut- (uty-) (sun, moon) rises; utn the east. To. wït- (wïty-) to increase (rain, wind), rise in pride; ut- (uty-) to increase (song-word; borrowed). Ka. uday(i)su, udisu to rise, be born. Tu. udiyuni, udipini to rise (as the sun), be generated; udipāvuni to beget; udi, udaya rising of the sun, moon, or other heavenly bodies; udupu act of coming into existence. Te. udayamu rising of the sun, etc.; udayincu to rise, be born. /Skt. ud-i to rise; vin. udaya-.

Ta. uttaravu answer, reply; order, command, grant, leave; uttaram answer, reply. Ma. uttaravu command, leave; uttaram answer; command, letter. Ko. utarv permission, order. L. V.R. 1934, 261.
Ta. utakam water; utakännam food and drink. Ma. udakam (d, not t) water. Ko. udk broth (esp. made from meat). Ka. udaka water. Tu. udaka id. Te. udakamu id. /Skt. udaka water.
